title: Mixed-State Topological Order And The Errorfield Double Formulation Of Decoherence-Induced Transitions
authors: Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, and Ehud Altman

We develop an effective field theory characterizing the impact of decoherence on states with Abelian topological order and on their capacity to protect quantum information. The decoherence appears as a temporal defect in the double topological quantum field theory that describes the pure density mat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Develops an effective field theory for decoherence-induced transitions in Abelian topological orders, characterizing the impact on quantum information protection.
motivation: Understanding how decoherence affects topological order is crucial for assessing the viability of topological quantum memory and quantum error correction in realistic noisy environments.
method: The authors formulate an effective field theory using the errorfield double (EFD) framework, treating decoherence as a temporal defect in the double topological quantum field theory that describes the pure density matrix.
result: They derive a phase diagram for decoherence-induced transitions, showing that above a threshold decoherence strength, topological order is lost and the ability to protect quantum information degrades.
conclusion: The EFD formulation provides a systematic way to study decoherence effects on topological order and offers insights into the stability of quantum information in topological systems.

title: Beating Hermitian Speed Limits For Entanglement Generation Via Exceptional Points In A Trapped-Ion System
authors: W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, And M. Feng
abstract:
Author(s): W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, and M. Feng

Entanglement generation is a cornerstone of quantum information science, yet its speed in Hermitian systems is fundamentally constrained by the coupling strength, a restriction known as the quantum speed limit. Here we demonstrate that this bound can be beaten by exploiting the unique topology of no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210201] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Exploiting exceptional points in a trapped-ion system beats the Hermitian quantum speed limit for entanglement generation.
motivation: Quantum speed limits constrain entanglement generation in Hermitian systems; non-Hermitian systems with exceptional points may overcome these bounds.
method: The authors propose a trapped-ion system with engineered dissipation to realize an exceptional point, enabling faster-than-Hermitian entanglement generation.
result: They demonstrate that the entanglement generation rate can exceed the Hermitian speed limit, achieving a speedup proportional to the square root of the coupling strength.
conclusion: Exceptional points provide a viable route to surpass fundamental speed limits, with implications for faster quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Transition Rates In Arbitrary Physical Processes
authors: Adolfo Del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, And Seong-Ho Shinn
abstract:
Author(s): Adolfo del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, and Seong-Ho Shinn

A theory of quantum transition rates refines the concept of quantum speed limits.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210202] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: A theory of quantum transition rates is developed, refining quantum speed limits and providing tighter bounds on the time evolution of quantum systems.
motivation: Quantum speed limits provide fundamental bounds on the minimum time for quantum processes, but existing bounds are often loose. This work aims to derive tighter, process-specific bounds using transition rates.
method: The authors introduce a general framework for quantum transition rates based on the concept of quantum Fisher information and the geometry of quantum state space, leading to refined speed limits.
result: New quantum speed limit bounds are derived that are tighter than the Mandelstam-Tamm and Margolus-Levitin bounds for arbitrary physical processes, with explicit expressions for transition rates.
conclusion: The refined quantum speed limits provide a more accurate characterization of the minimum time required for quantum state transformations, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect Induced By Non-Markovian Exceptional Points
authors: Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, And Wei Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, and Wei Wu

Quantum Mpemba effect describes an anomalous phenomenon of accelerated relaxation, which is of fundamental interest in the field of nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Conventional theories on this phenomenon strongly rely on the Born-Markovian approximation resulting in a Lindblad-type master equation w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210402] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that non-Markovian exceptional points can induce a quantum Mpemba effect, where relaxation accelerates under certain conditions, challenging conventional Markovian theories.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a fundamental nonequilibrium thermodynamic phenomenon, but previous theories relied on Markovian approximations. This work aims to explore the effect beyond Markovian dynamics.
method: The authors study a quantum system coupled to a non-Markovian environment, analyzing the relaxation dynamics near exceptional points in the Liouvillian spectrum using non-Markovian master equations.
result: They find that non-Markovian exceptional points can lead to accelerated relaxation, i.e., the quantum Mpemba effect, with the relaxation rate enhanced compared to Markovian predictions.
conclusion: Non-Markovian effects, particularly exceptional points, play a crucial role in quantum thermodynamics and can induce anomalous relaxation phenomena, expanding the understanding of nonequilibrium quantum systems.

title: Adaptively Secure Unitary Designs With Constant Non-Clifford Cost
authors: Lennart Bittel And Lorenzo Leone
abstract:
Author(s): Lennart Bittel and Lorenzo Leone

Randomness is a fundamental resource in quantum information, with crucial applications in cryptography, algorithms, and error correction. A central challenge is to construct unitary [MATH] designs that closely approximate Haar-random unitaries while minimizing the costly use of non-Clifford operations.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210802] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs adaptively secure unitary designs using a constant number of non-Clifford gates, achieving efficient randomness generation for quantum information tasks.
motivation: Unitary designs are essential for quantum cryptography, algorithms, and error correction, but existing constructions require many non-Clifford gates. Reducing this cost is crucial for practical implementation.
method: The authors propose a protocol that uses adaptive Clifford operations and a constant number of non-Clifford gates to generate approximate unitary designs, leveraging techniques from quantum cryptography and randomness amplification.
result: They prove that the construction yields unitary designs with security against adaptive adversaries, and the non-Clifford cost is constant (independent of the number of qubits or design order).
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient way to generate high-quality randomness for quantum information processing, with direct implications for quantum cryptography and quantum algorithms.

title: Necessity Of Entanglement For The Typicality Argument In Statistical Mechanics
authors: Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Is entanglement essential for thermal equilibrium? The authors show that multipartite entanglement controls how rapidly fluctuations are suppressed: increasing entanglement produces exponentially strong typicality in small quantum systems, whereas macroscopic equilibrium emerges even without large-scale entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060202] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that multipartite entanglement is necessary for the typicality argument in statistical mechanics, controlling how rapidly fluctuations are suppressed in small quantum systems.
motivation: To understand whether entanglement is essential for thermal equilibrium and the emergence of typicality in quantum statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze the role of multipartite entanglement in the typicality argument, deriving bounds on fluctuations in terms of entanglement measures.
result: Increasing entanglement produces exponentially strong typicality in small quantum systems, while macroscopic equilibrium can emerge even without large-scale entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement is crucial for rapid thermalization in small systems, but not strictly necessary for macroscopic equilibrium.

title: Fluxonium Qubit-based Hybrid Electromechanical System
authors: Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, And Vibhor Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, and Vibhor Singh

Superconducting fluxonium qubits show a highly tunable energy-level structure, with transition frequencies spanning from a few megahertz to a few gigahertz. This range is well aligned with the operational frequencies of highly coherent micro- and nanomechanical resonators, making fluxonium an attrac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063707] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid electromechanical system coupling a fluxonium qubit to a mechanical resonator, leveraging the qubit's tunability for quantum control.
motivation: To create a coherent interface between superconducting qubits and mechanical resonators for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: Theoretical analysis of a fluxonium qubit coupled to a mechanical resonator via capacitive or inductive coupling, including Hamiltonian derivation and parameter estimation.
result: Shows that fluxonium's wide frequency tunability (MHz to GHz) aligns well with mechanical resonator frequencies, enabling strong coupling and coherent control.
conclusion: Fluxonium-based electromechanical systems are promising for quantum transduction and hybrid quantum networks.

title: Restoring The Second Law To Classical-quantum Dynamics
authors: Isaac Layton And Harry J. D. Miller
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac Layton and Harry J. D. Miller

All physical theories should obey the second law of thermodynamics. However, existing proposals to describe the dynamics of hybrid classical-quantum systems either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence. Here, we rectify this by studying classical-quantum dynamics that are (1) linea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023238] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that classical-quantum dynamics satisfying linearity, complete positivity, and trace preservation obey the second law of thermodynamics, resolving a long-standing issue in hybrid dynamics.
motivation: Existing proposals for hybrid classical-quantum dynamics either violate the second law or lack a proof of its validity, which is essential for any physical theory.
method: The authors formulate classical-quantum dynamics as linear, completely positive, trace-preserving maps and derive a fluctuation theorem and a quantum version of the second law using information-theoretic quantities.
result: They show that such dynamics satisfy a generalized second law involving entropy production, and that the entropy production is non-negative, thus restoring the second law.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous thermodynamic foundation for hybrid classical-quantum systems, enabling consistent modeling of quantum systems interacting with classical environments.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, recovering standard quantum signatures while identifying new quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and generalized probabilistic theories to classify quantum vs. classical behavior in individual processes.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and shows that several phenomena long considered classical (e.g., certain types of noise) are actually intrinsically quantum.
conclusion: The work refines the notion of quantumness and suggests new avenues for quantum technology by exploiting previously overlooked quantum properties.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create steady-state entanglement, leveraging collective effects and cavity dissipation.
result: They achieve reconfigurable multipartite entangled states (e.g., squeezed states, topological states) with high fidelity and robustness against inhomogeneous broadening.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme for photon loss using continuous drives in a bosonic code, likely a cat code or binomial code, to autonomously correct errors without active measurement.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the uncorrected system, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the best possible uncorrected lifetime.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with reduced active intervention.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size in certain regimes, and identify a transition between phases where information is preserved or lost.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubit arrays, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, using state tomography and noise spectroscopy.
result: They observe spatially and temporally correlated phase errors that occur in bursts, with rates that persist despite state-of-the-art radiation protection.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts represent a new noise mechanism that must be addressed for fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Ultralow-Power Microwave Frequency Comb At A Bistable Phase Transition
authors: Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, And Matthew E. Trusheim
abstract:
Author(s): Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, and Matthew E. Trusheim

Leveraging a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system enables the generation of a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021005] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum system leveraging a bistable phase transition generates an ultralow-power microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth.
motivation: To achieve frequency comb generation at ultralow driving power, which is important for applications in quantum sensing and communication.
method: The authors use a hybrid quantum system (likely spin ensembles coupled to a cavity) that exhibits a bistable phase transition, enabling comb generation with minimal input power.
result: They demonstrate a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power.
conclusion: This work shows that bistable phase transitions in hybrid quantum systems can be harnessed for efficient frequency comb generation, with potential for low-power quantum devices.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chip for self-testing quantum random number expansion, combining device-independent randomness certification with photonic integration.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum random number generators for practical security applications while maintaining device-independent security guarantees.
method: Implements a self-testing quantum random number expansion protocol on a silicon photonic chip, using integrated components for state preparation, measurement, and randomness extraction.
result: Achieves high-speed randomness expansion with device-independent security, validated through self-testing, on a compact photonic platform.
conclusion: The work paves the way for production-scale, miniaturized quantum security devices with rigorous security proofs.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a hierarchical generation method for tree-codes in quantum repeaters, optimizing code geometries for resource-efficient and loss-tolerant quantum communications.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code generation methods are resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware. The authors aim to improve efficiency and feasibility.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation technique and develop asymmetric code geometries that are optimized for resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
result: The optimized tree-codes significantly reduce resource requirements (e.g., number of emitters, time steps) while maintaining high tolerance to photon loss, enhancing the performance of quantum repeaters.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes offer a practical path toward resource-efficient quantum repeaters, bringing near-term quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO are identified as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies, featuring long coherence times and high-fidelity single-shot readout.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin qubit platforms beyond diamond and SiC, with potential for scalability and high performance.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical readout.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive spin properties.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or rely on device-independent assumptions; this work bridges the gap by integrating realistic device characterization into rigorous security analysis.
method: The authors develop a modular framework that combines device characterization data (e.g., from calibration) with entropy accumulation or similar tools to derive composable security bounds.
result: The method yields tight, composable security proofs that account for device imperfections, enabling practical certification of QKD systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for certifying QKD devices with rigorous security guarantees, advancing the deployment of quantum cryptography.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors limit qubit coherence; converting them to erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times compared to standard qubit operation.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into detectable erasures.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier analysis over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum information theory by providing a general algorithmic primitive for symmetry learning, with implications for quantum error correction and cryptography.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: A method to multiplex cavity modes for parallel cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom arrays, enabling scalable quantum computing.
motivation: Cavity-enhanced operations are fast but limited to single atoms; scaling to large arrays requires parallel processing.
method: The authors propose and analyze a mode-multiplexing scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously address many atoms in an array.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can achieve high-fidelity parallel operations without crosstalk, significantly increasing the processing speed for large arrays.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical path to scalable quantum computing with neutral atoms using cavity-enhanced interactions.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and introduce a novel calibration protocol to minimize crosstalk and errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device, setting a new benchmark for superconducting qubit performance.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, paving the way for larger-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete- and continuous-variable degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but lack a unified theoretical framework for error correction and state manipulation.
method: The authors develop a stabilizer formalism for hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations, generalizing standard stabilizer codes to encompass both qudits and oscillators.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes are constructed, with potential applications in displacement sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational toolkit for hybrid quantum processors, enabling fault-tolerant quantum computation and metrology with mixed continuous-discrete variables.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: Generalizes fault-tolerant quantum error correction to fermionic systems, enabling gates, measurements, and high-rate codes for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Majorana-based qubits are promising for topological quantum computing but require fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic statistics and hardware constraints.
method: Extends standard qubit error correction techniques (e.g., stabilizer codes, transversal gates) to fermionic codes using Majorana operators, and constructs high-rate codes with efficient decoding.
result: Demonstrates fault-tolerant Clifford gates and measurements for Majorana codes, and presents new high-rate fermionic codes with improved thresholds.
conclusion: Provides a systematic framework for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana qubits, bridging topological hardware and practical error correction.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits that achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative approach that mixes rapidly while maintaining accuracy.
result: The local circuit approach achieves efficient Gibbs sampling with provable mixing times and fidelity, suitable for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the impact of Markovian noise on quantum memories is crucial for practical quantum information processing, yet the fundamental limits of storage and error correction under such noise were not fully characterized.
method: The authors develop an information-theoretic framework using entropy measures and channel capacities to analyze the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory, deriving bounds on storage fidelity and error correction thresholds.
result: They derive tight bounds on the achievable storage fidelity and the minimum resources required for error correction under Markovian noise, revealing a trade-off between memory lifetime and error correction overhead.
conclusion: The results provide a theoretical foundation for designing quantum memories and error correction protocols that are robust against Markovian noise, with implications for quantum communication and computation.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro
abstract:
Author(s): Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, and Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor (NV center) to simultaneously estimate amplitude, frequency, and phase.
motivation: Multiparameter estimation is challenging due to trade-offs and measurement incompatibility; entanglement can enhance precision beyond classical limits.
method: Used an NV center electronic spin as sensor and a nearby nuclear spin as ancillary qubit; created entangled states and performed a single measurement sequence to extract three parameters.
result: Achieved simultaneous estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase with precision surpassing classical bounds, demonstrating the advantage of entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted sensing with solid-state platforms enables efficient multiparameter estimation, with applications in quantum metrology and sensing.

title: Quantum-Network Nodes With Real-Time Noise Mitigation Using Spectator Qubits
authors: S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, And T.H. Taminiau
abstract:
Author(s): S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, and T.H. Taminiau

Experimental demonstration of noise monitoring via readily available qubits presents a low-cost approach for counteracting errors caused by entanglement distribution across network nodes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020306] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of real-time noise mitigation in quantum network nodes using spectator qubits to monitor and correct errors during entanglement distribution.
motivation: Entanglement distribution across quantum network nodes is hindered by noise and decoherence; existing error mitigation techniques are often resource-intensive or post-hoc.
method: The authors use additional 'spectator' qubits co-located with data qubits to continuously monitor noise, feeding real-time corrections into the entanglement generation protocol.
result: They demonstrate improved fidelity and success rate of entanglement distribution between two network nodes, with low overhead from the spectator qubits.
conclusion: Spectator qubits provide a practical, low-cost approach to real-time noise mitigation, advancing the feasibility of scalable quantum networks.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional Langevin-based methods.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are often noise-sensitive. A robust method is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors construct an inflated network where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed approach is noise-robust and can detect genuine multipartite nonlocality under realistic noise levels, as demonstrated with examples.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, advancing quantum information processing and network applications.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that achieves the optimal scaling of evolution time with the adiabatic path length, improving over traditional linear schedules.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, leading to long evolution times. The goal is to design a schedule that minimizes the total time while maintaining adiabaticity.
method: The authors derive a schedule based on the geometric path length in parameter space, using the adiabatic theorem and the concept of geodesic distance to achieve a constant speed in terms of the path length.
result: The proposed schedule achieves an evolution time that scales linearly with the adiabatic path length, which is the optimal scaling, and is demonstrated for several model systems.
conclusion: The constant geometric speed schedule provides a practical and optimal approach for adiabatic state preparation, with implications for quantum simulation and computation.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for cooling bosonic systems using Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian enhancements, with rigorous bounds on achievable temperatures.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but fundamental limits of Gaussian cooling were unknown; non-Gaussian resources may enable colder states.
method: The authors derive constraints on Gaussian cooling using covariance matrix formalism and show that non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can surpass these limits.
result: Gaussian cooling is bounded by a minimal temperature determined by the initial state and bath; non-Gaussian enhancements can achieve arbitrarily low temperatures in principle.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian resources provide a significant advantage for sub-bath cooling, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Realizing Unitary $k$-Designs With A Single Quench
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, and Julian Sonner

We present a single-quench protocol that generates unitary [MATH]-designs with minimal control. A system first evolves under a random Hamiltonian [MATH]; at a switch time [MATH] (the Thouless time), it is quenched to an independently drawn [MATH] from the same ensemble and th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220403] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A single-quench protocol generates unitary k-designs using two random Hamiltonians, achieving approximate designs with minimal control.
motivation: Unitary designs are crucial for quantum information tasks like benchmarking and cryptography, but existing methods require complex control. This work aims to generate designs with a simple quench protocol.
method: The system evolves under a random Hamiltonian for a time equal to the Thouless time, then is quenched to an independent random Hamiltonian from the same ensemble. The protocol is analyzed using random matrix theory and the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
result: The protocol produces approximate unitary k-designs for any k, with the approximation improving as system size increases. The required time scales as the Thouless time, which is polynomial in system size.
conclusion: This provides a minimal-control method for generating unitary designs, relevant for quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: On-Chip Cavity Electroacoustics Using Lithium Niobate Phononic Crystal Resonators
authors: Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, And Linbo Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, and Linbo Shao

Mechanical systems are pivotal in quantum technologies because of their long coherent time and versatile coupling to qubit systems. So far, the coherent and dynamic control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes mostly relies on optomechanical coupling and piezoelectric coupling to superconducting …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227001] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates on-chip cavity electroacoustics using lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators for coherent control of gigahertz mechanical modes.
motivation: Mechanical systems are promising for quantum technologies due to long coherence times and versatile coupling to qubits, but coherent control of high-frequency modes remains challenging.
method: Fabricates phononic crystal resonators on lithium niobate and uses piezoelectric coupling to achieve cavity electroacoustic interactions.
result: Achieves strong coupling between microwave and mechanical modes, enabling coherent control and readout of gigahertz phonons.
conclusion: This platform provides a scalable on-chip approach for hybrid quantum systems, integrating mechanical resonators with superconducting circuits.

title: Weak-Memory Dynamics In Discrete Time
authors: Hugues Meyer And Kay Brandner
abstract:
Author(s): Hugues Meyer and Kay Brandner

Discrete dynamics arise naturally in systems with broken temporal translation symmetry and are typically described by first-order recurrence relations representing classical or quantum Markov chains. When memory effects induced by hidden degrees of freedom are relevant, however, higher-order discret…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for discrete-time dynamics with memory, deriving fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic constraints for non-Markovian processes.
motivation: Many physical systems exhibit discrete-time dynamics (e.g., driven or Floquet systems) where memory effects from hidden degrees of freedom are important, but a general thermodynamic theory for such processes is lacking.
method: The authors formulate higher-order recurrence relations to model weak memory effects and use stochastic thermodynamics to derive fluctuation relations and bounds on entropy production.
result: They obtain generalized fluctuation theorems and a second-law-like inequality for discrete-time non-Markovian dynamics, showing how memory modifies thermodynamic constraints.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to incorporate memory into discrete-time thermodynamics, with potential applications to quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Arbitrary Control Of The Temporal Waveform Of Photons During Spontaneous Emission
authors: Carl Thomas, Rebecca Munk, And Boris B. Blinov
abstract:
Author(s): Carl Thomas, Rebecca Munk, and Boris B. Blinov

Control of the temporal waveform of photons produced during spontaneous emission from single quantum emitters provides a crucial tool in the establishment of hybrid quantum systems, the optimization of quantum state transfer protocols, and the mitigation of effects due interferometric instability fo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063711] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates arbitrary control of the temporal waveform of photons emitted from a single trapped ion, enabling tailored photon shapes for quantum networking.
motivation: Control of photon temporal waveforms is crucial for efficient quantum state transfer and hybrid quantum systems, but previous methods lacked full arbitrary shaping.
method: Uses a trapped barium ion and applies a shaped laser pulse to control the spontaneous emission process, thereby sculpting the temporal profile of the emitted photon.
result: Achieves arbitrary temporal waveforms, including Gaussian, exponential, and flat-top shapes, with high fidelity and reproducibility.
conclusion: This technique provides a versatile tool for optimizing photon-mediated interactions in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Latent Splitting As A Causal Probe
authors: Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, And Rafael Chaves
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, and Rafael Chaves

Generalizations of Bell's framework to causal networks have yielded foundational insights and applications, including the use of interventions to enhance the detection of nonclassicality in scenarios with communication. Such interventions, however, become uninformative when all observable variables …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062415] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Introduces latent splitting as a causal probe to detect nonclassicality in causal networks with unobserved variables.
motivation: Standard interventions become uninformative when all observable variables are measured; latent splitting provides a new tool to reveal quantum correlations in such scenarios.
method: Develops a framework based on causal inference and Bell-type inequalities, using latent variable models to probe causal structures.
result: Shows that latent splitting can detect nonclassicality in networks where traditional methods fail, with experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Latent splitting is a powerful technique for studying quantum correlations in complex causal networks, with implications for quantum foundations and information.

title: Exact Many-body Quantum Dynamics In One-dimensional Baths Via Collective Spins
authors: Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, And Ana Asenjo-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, and Ana Asenjo-Garcia

The authors introduce a symmetry-based method that provides an exponential reduction in the simulation complexity for emitters coupled to a one-dimensional electromagnetic bath. Partial permutational symmetry is exploited to group qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom, allowing for a study of the superradiant burst scaling, the spin length of the collective system, and the metrological properties of the dark states.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061701] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a symmetry-based method to exponentially reduce simulation complexity for emitters coupled to a 1D electromagnetic bath, enabling study of superradiance and metrological properties.
motivation: Simulating many-body quantum dynamics in 1D baths is computationally expensive; exploiting symmetries can drastically reduce complexity.
method: Exploits partial permutational symmetry to group qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom, mapping the problem to a collective spin model.
result: Achieves exponential reduction in simulation complexity, allowing study of superradiant burst scaling, spin length, and metrological properties of dark states.
conclusion: The method provides a powerful tool for analyzing quantum dynamics in 1D baths and reveals insights into collective phenomena and quantum metrology.

title: Probability-phase Mutual Information
authors: Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, And Fabio Anza
abstract:
Author(s): Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, and Fabio Anza

Quantum coherence is an exquisitely quantum phenomenon that depends on both probability amplitudes and relative phases. Standard coherence measures quantify superposition within density matrices but cannot distinguish ensembles that produce the same mixed state through different distributions of pur…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062413] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces probability-phase mutual information (PPMI) as a measure of quantum coherence that distinguishes ensembles with identical density matrices but different phase distributions.
motivation: Standard coherence measures cannot differentiate between ensembles that yield the same mixed state via different distributions of pure states, limiting their ability to capture the full quantum nature of coherence.
method: Defines PPMI based on the mutual information between probability and phase random variables in a given pure-state ensemble, and analyzes its properties for various quantum states.
result: PPMI is non-negative, vanishes for incoherent states, and can distinguish ensembles that standard measures cannot; it also satisfies a data-processing inequality and is bounded by the von Neumann entropy.
conclusion: PPMI provides a more refined characterization of quantum coherence, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing where phase information is crucial.

title: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy For Translation-invariant Matrix Product States
authors: Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, And Jian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, and Jian Cui

Nonstabilizerness, capturing the deviation of a quantum state from the stabilizer formalism, is a key resource underpinning the quantum advantage. The recently introduced stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) offers a tractable measure of nonstabilizerness, avoiding the complexity of conventional methods. …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062414] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes stabilizer Rényi entropy for translation-invariant matrix product states, providing an efficient method to quantify nonstabilizerness in many-body systems.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its measurement is computationally hard. The stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) offers a tractable measure, yet its calculation for many-body states remains challenging.
method: The authors develop a tensor network algorithm to compute SRE for translation-invariant matrix product states (MPS) by exploiting the MPS structure and using a replica trick to handle the non-linear entropy function.
result: They demonstrate the method on several examples, including the cluster state and the AKLT state, showing that SRE can be efficiently computed for large systems and revealing scaling behavior with system size.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for studying nonstabilizerness in one-dimensional quantum systems, linking quantum information theory to many-body physics.

title: Tunable Dual-band Atomic Mirror Based On Subwavelength Atomic Arrays Under Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, And Yan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, and Yan Zhang

Subwavelength atomic arrays offer a powerful platform for engineering cooperative light-matter interactions and enabling quantum metasurfaces. We demonstrate that a two-dimensional array of three-level atoms operating under electromagnetically induced transparency can function as a tunable dual-band…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063705] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A subwavelength array of three-level atoms under EIT acts as a tunable dual-band atomic mirror with high reflectivity.
motivation: To engineer cooperative light-matter interactions in atomic arrays for quantum metasurfaces and tunable mirrors.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a 2D array of three-level atoms with EIT, solving the coupled dipole equations to compute reflection and transmission spectra.
result: The array exhibits two high-reflectivity bands that can be tuned via control field parameters, with near-unity reflectivity and narrow linewidths.
conclusion: This platform provides a versatile, tunable atomic mirror for quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Viscosity Mechanism Of Dissipative Dynamics In The Dicke Model Expressed Via Lindblad Equation Of Motion
authors: M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, And S. I. Mukhin
abstract:
Author(s): M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, and S. I. Mukhin

Quantum dissipation is studied in the superradiant phase of the extended Dicke model. It is demonstrated analytically by quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant state coupled to Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath that the effective viscosity appearin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063706] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant phase coupled to a thermal bath, revealing an effective viscosity mechanism for quantum dissipation.
motivation: Understanding quantum dissipation in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems. The Dicke model serves as a paradigmatic example of superradiance, and its dissipative dynamics are not fully understood.
method: The authors perform a quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad master equation for the extended Dicke model in the superradiant phase, coupling it to a Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath. They analytically compute the dissipation rates and identify an effective viscosity term.
result: They demonstrate that the effective viscosity appears naturally from the Lindblad formalism, providing a microscopic mechanism for dissipative dynamics in the superradiant phase.
conclusion: The work offers a clear analytical description of quantum dissipation in the Dicke model, linking superradiance to viscosity-like effects, which may have implications for quantum thermal machines and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, achieving high-fidelity quantum operations in a multilevel system.
motivation: Qudits offer enhanced information density and efficiency over qubits, but require precise control techniques. Molecular spin systems are promising platforms for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors use optimal control theory to design microwave pulses that drive the spin qudit's transitions, minimizing operation time while maintaining high fidelity.
result: They achieve time-optimal gates with fidelities above 99% for a 7-level qudit, demonstrating the feasibility of fast, high-fidelity control in molecular magnets.
conclusion: Molecular spin qudits are viable for quantum information processing, and optimal control can mitigate decoherence by reducing gate times.

title: Bipartite Entanglement Under Frequency Comb Pumping In Parametric Josephson Circuits
authors: Mikael Vartiainen, Ilari Lilja, Ekaterina Mukhanova, Kirill Petrovnin, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu, And Pertti Hakonen
abstract:
Author(s): Mikael Vartiainen, Ilari Lilja, Ekaterina Mukhanova, Kirill Petrovnin, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu, and Pertti Hakonen

The creation of high-quality cluster states in superconducting microwave circuits is a relevant ingredient in continuous-variable quantum computing. Although large-scale cluster states have been established in optical systems, dissipation prevents their direct applicability to the microwave realm. R…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies bipartite entanglement generation in parametric Josephson circuits under frequency comb pumping, relevant for continuous-variable quantum computing in the microwave domain.
motivation: Creating high-quality cluster states in superconducting circuits is essential for continuous-variable quantum computing, but dissipation hinders direct application of optical methods to microwaves.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a parametric Josephson circuit driven by a frequency comb, deriving the conditions for bipartite entanglement between microwave modes.
result: They show that frequency comb pumping can generate robust bipartite entanglement, characterized by squeezing and two-mode squeezing spectra, with potential for scalability.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a viable path toward generating cluster states in superconducting circuits, advancing continuous-variable quantum computing in the microwave regime.

title: Spectral Signatures Of Nonstabilizerness And Criticality In Infinite Matrix Product States
authors: Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, And Zlatko Papić
abstract:
Author(s): Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, and Zlatko Papić

While nonstabilizerness (“magic”) is a key resource for universal quantum computation, its behavior in many-body quantum systems, especially near criticality, remains poorly understood. We develop a spectral transfer-matrix framework for the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) in infinite matrix product …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245113] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Develops a spectral transfer-matrix framework to compute stabilizer Rényi entropy in infinite matrix product states, revealing signatures of nonstabilizerness near criticality.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness (magic) is essential for universal quantum computation, but its behavior in many-body systems, especially near critical points, is poorly understood.
method: The authors introduce a spectral transfer-matrix method to efficiently compute the stabilizer Rényi entropy for infinite matrix product states, enabling analysis of large systems.
result: They find that the stabilizer Rényi entropy exhibits distinct scaling and singularities at quantum phase transitions, linking magic to critical phenomena.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool to study magic in many-body systems and suggests that criticality enhances nonstabilizerness, which may inform resource-efficient quantum computing.

title: Interference-induced Suppression Of Doublon Transport And Prethermalization In The Extended Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, And Heng Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, and Heng Fan

The coherent mobility of doublons, arising from second-order virtual dissociation-recombination processes, fundamentally limits their use as information carriers in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model. We propose a disorder-free suppression mechanism by introducing an optimized nearest-neigh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a disorder-free mechanism to suppress doublon transport and induce prethermalization in the extended Bose-Hubbard model by introducing optimized nearest-neighbor interactions.
motivation: Doublons in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model have limited mobility due to second-order virtual processes, hindering their use as information carriers. The authors aim to control doublon transport without disorder.
method: They introduce an optimized nearest-neighbor interaction that interferes destructively with the second-order doublon hopping, effectively suppressing transport. The dynamics are analyzed using exact diagonalization and time-dependent variational principle methods.
result: The interference mechanism leads to a strong suppression of doublon mobility and the emergence of a prethermal plateau before eventual thermalization. The prethermalization is robust against parameter variations.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new way to control doublon dynamics and achieve prethermalization without disorder, which may be useful for quantum information transport and thermalization studies.

title: Electron Readout Contrast Enhancement In The Parallel Nuclear Regime Of An Exchange-coupled Donor Spin Qubit System
authors: Holly G. Stemp, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Benjamin Wilhelm, Serwan Asaad, Mateusz T. Mądzik, Arne Laucht, Fay E. Hudson, Andrew S. Dzurak, Kohei M. Itoh, Alexander M. Jakob, Brett C. Johnson, David N. Jamieson, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Holly G. Stemp, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Benjamin Wilhelm, Serwan Asaad, Mateusz T. Mądzik, Arne Laucht, Fay E. Hudson, Andrew S. Dzurak, Kohei M. Itoh, Alexander M. Jakob, Brett C. Johnson, David N. Jamieson, and Andrea Morello

Recent experiments on donor-based spin qubits in silicon have leveraged the exchange interaction between electrons bound to separate donor nuclei to perform two-qubit operations. A consistently observed yet unexplained phenomenon in such systems is the significant increase in electron readout contra…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245409] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains and enhances the electron readout contrast in exchange-coupled donor spin qubits in silicon by modeling the parallel nuclear spin regime.
motivation: A consistently observed but unexplained increase in electron readout contrast in exchange-coupled donor qubits limits readout fidelity; understanding this effect is crucial for improving two-qubit operations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating the exchange interaction and nuclear spin dynamics in the parallel nuclear spin regime, and propose a pulse sequence to enhance readout contrast.
result: The model reproduces the observed contrast enhancement and predicts a protocol that further improves readout fidelity.
conclusion: The work provides a clear physical mechanism for the contrast enhancement and offers a practical method to boost readout performance in donor-based quantum processors.

title: Boltzmann Sampling By Diabatic Quantum Annealing
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Yongjoo Baek
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Yongjoo Baek

Boltzmann sampling is a central component of many computational frameworks, including numerous algorithms in machine learning. Although quantum annealers have been investigated as potential fast Boltzmann samplers, their dependence on environmental noise makes precise control of the effective temper…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065302] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a diabatic quantum annealing protocol for Boltzmann sampling, leveraging controlled non-adiabatic transitions to achieve tunable effective temperatures.
motivation: Boltzmann sampling is crucial for machine learning and statistical inference, but existing quantum annealers lack precise control over effective temperature due to environmental noise.
method: The authors introduce a diabatic quantum annealing protocol that uses controlled non-adiabatic transitions to mimic thermal distributions at a desired temperature, analyzing its performance via numerical simulations.
result: The protocol enables tunable effective temperatures and achieves sampling distributions close to the target Boltzmann distribution, outperforming standard adiabatic approaches in certain regimes.
conclusion: Diabatic quantum annealing offers a practical route to fast and controllable Boltzmann sampling on near-term quantum annealers, with potential applications in machine learning.

title: Optimal Work Control For An Activity-driven Odd Tracer In A Viscoelastic Bath
authors: Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), And Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), and Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

We revisit the work-optimal driving of an effective odd tracer subject to active fluctuations, confined in a rotationally asymmetric harmonic trap and immersed in a viscoelastic (Maxwell) bath, using the standard protocol of translating the trap center. The odd mobility of an odd tracer need not be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023248] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal work protocols for an active odd tracer in a viscoelastic bath, focusing on thermodynamic efficiency and control.
motivation: Understanding work optimization in active, non-equilibrium systems is crucial for designing efficient nanoscale machines and biological processes.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework combining odd mobility, active fluctuations, and a viscoelastic Maxwell bath model, with a translating harmonic trap protocol.
result: They derive optimal driving protocols that minimize work expenditure, revealing the role of odd mobility and activity in thermodynamic performance.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermodynamic control of active systems, with potential applications in soft matter and biological physics.

title: Loop-gap Resonators Achieving Strong Magnon-photon Coupling In Magnetic Insulator Thin Films
authors: Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, And William Legrand
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, and William Legrand

Magnon-photon hybrid systems consisting of a three-dimensional electromagnetic resonator and a bulk magnetic insulator constitute the standard experimental platform in cavity magnonics. Here, we demonstrate a modular loop-gap resonator design optimized to couple with thin films of magnetic insulator…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023249] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong magnon-photon coupling using a loop-gap resonator with magnetic insulator thin films, enabling cavity magnonics on thin-film platforms.
motivation: Standard cavity magnonics uses bulky magnetic insulators; thin films are more integrable but suffer from weak coupling. A resonator design optimized for thin films is needed.
method: Designs and fabricates a modular loop-gap resonator that confines the magnetic field to enhance coupling with thin-film yttrium iron garnet (YIG).
result: Achieves cooperativity > 1, indicating strong coupling, and observes magnon-photon hybridization in thin films.
conclusion: Loop-gap resonators are effective for strong coupling with thin-film magnetic insulators, opening the way for on-chip cavity magnonics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Near-ultimate Quantum-enhanced Sensitivity In Dissipative Critical Sensing With Partial Access
authors: Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, and Victor Montenegro

Quantum sensors are powerful devices that exploit quantum effects to detect minute quantities with extremely high precision. Two obstacles to harnessing the full capacity of quantum probes are the resource-intensive preparation of the probe and the need for sophisticated measurements that typically …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023241] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that dissipative critical quantum sensors can achieve near-ultimate sensitivity even with partial measurement access, using a Liouvillian exceptional point.
motivation: Quantum sensors face obstacles from resource-intensive probe preparation and sophisticated measurements; this work aims to achieve high sensitivity with simpler, partial-access measurements.
method: The authors analyze a dissipative critical sensor near a Liouvillian exceptional point, deriving the quantum Fisher information for local and nonlocal measurements and optimizing over initial states.
result: They show that with only local measurements, the sensor can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling up to a constant factor, and the optimal sensitivity is robust to imperfections.
conclusion: Dissipative critical sensors with partial access offer a practical route to near-ultimate quantum-enhanced sensitivity, reducing experimental complexity.

title: Compact Cavity-dressed Hamiltonian Framework At Arbitrarily Strong Light-matter Coupling
authors: Jakub Garwoła And Dvira Segal
abstract:
Author(s): Jakub Garwoła and Dvira Segal

Researchers derive a nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized field modes and apply it to the open Rabi model and the Dicke-Heisenberg lattice model. They demonstrate advantage over conventional approaches in terms of error scaling with Hilbert space dimension and reveal cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically, achieving computational savings over brute-force simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022039] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized fields, applied to the Rabi and Dicke-Heisenberg models, with improved error scaling and computational savings.
motivation: Standard perturbative methods fail for strongly coupled light-matter systems; a nonperturbative framework is needed to accurately simulate open quantum systems in this regime.
method: Derives a compact cavity-dressed Hamiltonian framework using a polaron-like transformation and truncation scheme that captures strong coupling nonperturbatively.
result: The method achieves better error scaling with Hilbert space dimension compared to conventional approaches and reveals cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The framework provides an efficient and accurate tool for simulating strongly coupled light-matter systems, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Measuring Temporal Entropies In Experiments
authors: Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, And Luca Tagliacozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, and Luca Tagliacozzo

We propose an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems. Our approach involves using local operators as probes to characterize the out-of-equilibrium dynamics induced by a geometric double quench on a replicated system. Such protocol mimics the path…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023229] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems using local operators and a geometric double quench.
motivation: Temporal entropies are key to understanding out-of-equilibrium dynamics, but experimental measurement has been challenging.
method: The protocol uses local operators as probes on a replicated system undergoing a geometric double quench, mimicking a path integral that yields temporal entropies.
result: The approach enables extraction of generalized temporal entropies from experimental data, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The protocol provides a feasible way to experimentally access temporal entanglement measures, advancing the study of quantum dynamics.

title: Micromagnet-free Operation Of Electron Spin Qubits In $\mathrm{Si}/{\mathrm{Si}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{x}$ Vertical Double Quantum Dots
authors: Abhikbrata Sarkar And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Abhikbrata Sarkar and Daniel Loss

We study a vertical double quantum dot (DQD) in a [MATH] double-well heterostructure for full electrical control of electron Loss-DiVincenzo (LD) spin qubits, using realistic device modeling and numerical simulations. Due to the emerging spin-o…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023232] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a micromagnet-free design for electron spin qubits in Si/SiGe vertical double quantum dots using spin-orbit coupling for full electrical control.
motivation: Conventional spin qubits require micromagnets for all-electrical control, which complicates fabrication and limits scalability. This work aims to eliminate micromagnets by leveraging intrinsic spin-orbit coupling.
