method: Realistic device modeling and numerical simulations of a vertical double quantum dot in a Si/SiGe heterostructure, analyzing the spin-orbit coupling and its effect on qubit operations.
result: Demonstrates that spin-orbit coupling in the vertical DQD enables fast, high-fidelity single-qubit gates without micromagnets, with gate fidelities exceeding 99%.
conclusion: The micromagnet-free approach simplifies qubit fabrication and is promising for scalable quantum computing in silicon.

title: Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks: Learning Dissipative Dynamics Via Contact Variational Principles
authors: Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, And Gang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, and Gang Yan

Physics-informed machine learning has proven effective for learning conservative dynamical systems. However, most real-world systems are nonconservative, and current approaches typically handle dissipation through ad hoc modifications or require access to full-state information. Here, we introduce t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023224] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks, a physics-informed machine learning framework for learning dissipative dynamics using contact variational principles.
motivation: Most real-world systems are nonconservative, and existing physics-informed ML methods handle dissipation via ad hoc modifications or require full-state information.
method: The method embeds Herglotz's contact variational principle into neural network architectures, enabling the learning of dissipative dynamics without explicit dissipation terms.
result: The approach accurately learns dissipative dynamics from data, outperforming standard neural ODEs and Lagrangian neural networks on benchmark systems.
conclusion: Contact variational principles provide a principled way to incorporate dissipation into physics-informed neural networks, offering a new tool for modeling nonconservative systems.

title: Impossibility Of Quantum Private Queries
authors: Esther Hänggi And Severin Winkler
abstract:
Author(s): Esther Hänggi and Severin Winkler

This work investigates whether quantum communication protocols allow confidential access to a remote database. It shows that any protocol that does not reveal which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022036] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that any quantum protocol for private database queries that hides which item is retrieved necessarily allows the user to reconstruct the entire database, establishing a fundamental impossibility.
motivation: Private queries allow a user to retrieve an item from a database without revealing which item was accessed. The goal is to determine if quantum communication can provide security beyond classical limitations.
method: The authors analyze general quantum protocols for private queries, using information-theoretic arguments to show that if the protocol is correct and the user's privacy is protected, then the user can recover the entire database.
result: Any quantum protocol that satisfies both correctness and user privacy (the server does not learn which item is retrieved) enables the user to reconstruct the entire database, implying that perfect quantum private queries are impossible.
conclusion: Quantum communication cannot circumvent the fundamental trade-off between user privacy and database security in private query protocols; the impossibility is information-theoretic.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A trapped-ion experiment demonstrates generation of arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states, including squeezed and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are essential for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered dissipation to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They successfully generate superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical nature through Wigner function tomography.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile method for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, enabling advances in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom components but suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and optimize the protocol parameters for high key rates over fiber.
result: The protocol achieves record-high secret key rates for CV-QKD over metropolitan distances, with rigorous composable security guarantees.
conclusion: This work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by simultaneously achieving high rates and strong security, making it a promising candidate for future quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is crucial for improving qubit readout.
motivation: Understanding how transmon qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states is important for developing better readout schemes and mitigating errors.
method: The authors probe transmon ionization by studying multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, likely using experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: They reveal the dynamics of transmon ionization, identifying key mechanisms that lead to qubit leakage.
conclusion: These insights can inform the design of improved readout protocols and error mitigation strategies for superconducting qubits.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing, especially for Trotterized dynamics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze the shadowing time and thermalization time in many-body chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition is generically a finite-size effect, not a true phase transition.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the breakdown of shadowing in quantum circuits, with implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A model reduction technique for open quantum systems based on measurement-adapted time-coarse graining that captures observable dynamics at the resolution of measurement channels.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduced model that preserves relevant dynamics is needed for efficient analysis.
method: The authors introduce a coarse-graining procedure that adapts to the time resolution of measurement channels, effectively projecting the full dynamics onto a lower-dimensional subspace that retains observable features.
result: The method is demonstrated on examples, showing accurate reproduction of measurement outcomes with significantly reduced computational cost.
conclusion: Measurement-adapted time-coarse graining provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems, bridging the gap between full quantum dynamics and effective models.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance, protecting qubits from thermal backaction and enabling scalable isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum computers.
motivation: Superconducting qubit readout requires low-noise amplification, but conventional isolators introduce loss and scalability issues. This work aims to eliminate isolators by integrating reverse isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier using Josephson junctions, incorporating passive reverse isolation through directional couplers or similar structures to suppress backaction from the output port.
result: The amplifier demonstrates near-quantum-limited noise performance while providing high reverse isolation, protecting qubits from thermal noise and enabling readout without external isolators.
conclusion: This amplifier architecture offers a practical path to scalable, isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum processors, improving system integration and performance.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how random measurements in a monitored quantum circuit can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, linking measurement-induced phenomena to coding theory.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between measurements and quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in the context of monitored dynamics where measurement outcomes can be used to improve decoding.
method: The authors analyze a family of random quantum circuits with intermediate measurements, modeling them as quantum codes and studying the stability of encoded information under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can significantly improve decodability, and they characterize the conditions under which monitored dynamics yield good quantum codes.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a new perspective on fault tolerance, suggesting that measurement-induced phases can be harnessed for error correction.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work aims to achieve strong blockade using collective effects in an ensemble.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that photon blockade strengthens with system size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission, even when individual emitters are weakly coupled.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action formalism combined with computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling systematic improvement of control fidelity.
result: The new method yields higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving, demonstrated on model systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique uses classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or target only independent noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling cancellation of k-local correlated noise using sequences whose length depends only on k, not the total number of qubits.
result: They demonstrate that the sequence length is determined solely by the locality of the noise, achieving efficient decoupling for large qubit arrays.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a scalable approach to noise mitigation in multi-qubit systems.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it is crucial for reaching the standard quantum limit and beyond.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, achieving orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for high-precision Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps to reduce the effective simulation error, thereby lowering the overall gate count in phase estimation.
result: They demonstrate that the new approach yields orders-of-magnitude resource savings compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation for benchmark quantum chemistry problems.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and efficient way to implement phase estimation on near-term quantum devices, significantly reducing the overhead of Hamiltonian simulation.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, achieving 99.61% readout fidelity for qudits.
motivation: Quantum measurements often disturb the system, limiting the ability to perform repeated or nondemolition measurements, especially in multilevel systems like spin qudits.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to minimize back-action and improve fidelity.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% for a spin qudit, reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique for high-fidelity, nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qudit platforms.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength, and characterize the spectral properties of the code.
conclusion: The work provides a simple mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, and use it as a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when simulating variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally achieve suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence and fidelity.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical method to mitigate leakage in spin qubits, advancing the viability of silicon-based quantum processors.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and complexity in many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors develop a framework based on process tensors and projected ensembles to probe chaos through repeated interventions, linking to out-of-time-order correlators and spectral statistics.
result: They demonstrate that the projected ensemble of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics and provide a unified perspective on existing chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: This approach offers a new tool for analyzing quantum chaos in open and closed systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves fundamental lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates needed to generate pseudorandom unitaries, showing that extensive doping is necessary.
motivation: Understanding the resource cost of generating pseudorandom unitaries is crucial for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage experiments, where Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates are a leading candidate.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including the concept of stabilizer entropy and the structure of the Clifford group, to derive lower bounds on the non-Clifford gate count for achieving approximate unitary designs.
result: They show that to achieve a unitary 2-design, the number of non-Clifford gates must scale linearly with the number of qubits, and for higher designs the scaling is even more demanding.
conclusion: The results establish fundamental limitations on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries with doped Clifford circuits, guiding the design of practical quantum protocols.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of a minimal Kitaev chain device, resolving parity dynamics essential for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems to resolve parity and key processes.
method: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry is applied to a minimal Kitaev chain device, enabling readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems.
result: The technique resolves key processes and parity dynamics, demonstrating a viable readout method for Kitaev chain qubits.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry provides a fast, noninvasive readout suitable for Majorana-based qubits, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, and Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020308] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control via shared control lines incurs only logarithmic overhead, making it efficient for scaling quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires many control lines, which is challenging. The authors investigate whether time-multiplexing (serializing control) can reduce hardware complexity without prohibitive overhead.
method: The authors analyze quantum circuits with time-multiplexed control, modeling the overhead in terms of gate count and circuit depth for various qubit topologies and gate configurations.
result: The overhead scales only logarithmically with the number of qubits, and for certain two-qubit gate configurations, there is no overhead at all.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable strategy for scaling quantum processors, as the serialization cost is minimal and can even vanish for specific gate sets.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer conceptual and practical advantages over discrete-variable methods for quantum communication, including compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.
method: The paper reviews theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, security proofs) and experimental progress in CV-QKD, CV quantum networks, and related protocols.
result: CV quantum communication is now as mature as discrete-variable approaches, with high-rate QKD demonstrations and network implementations.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and promising path for scalable quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in long-distance transmission and integration with quantum repeaters.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To classify and assess the security of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper provides a systematic classification of quantum crypto primitives, discusses their security definitions, and reviews experimental photonic implementations.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic tasks and evaluates their theoretical security and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers enhanced security for many primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors use nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that guides future experiments and theory in driven open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing long-coherence spin qubits, which are key for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing and can guide the design of spin qubits with improved coherence, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical or conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts (e.g., entanglement) and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments for gravitationally induced entanglement.
result: Gravitationally induced entanglement experiments are feasible with current or near-future technology and can test the quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Quantum information methods provide a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with several promising experimental proposals.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays
authors: Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, and Philipp M. Preiss

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with high fidelity, enabling quantum simulation and computing.
motivation: Neutral atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum information processing, but fermionic species pose challenges due to their internal state structure and interactions.
method: Uses optical tweezers with spin-resolved imaging and parallelized Raman sideband cooling to prepare arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic atoms in the motional ground state.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for arrays of up to 12 atoms, with deterministic loading and spin-state control.
conclusion: This work establishes fermionic tweezer arrays as a viable platform for quantum simulation and computing, with high-fidelity state preparation and readout.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, limiting prethermal plateaus.
motivation: Understanding how disorder protects against heating in driven quantum systems is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases.
method: The authors study a disordered spin chain under two-frequency periodic driving using numerical simulations and analytical arguments.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the disorder-induced prethermal plateau, leading to rapid heating even in the presence of strong disorder.
conclusion: Prethermalization in disordered Floquet systems is fragile to multi-frequency driving, which has implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamic control.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact quantum master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, using an equation-of-motion approach.
motivation: Exact master equations for multistate and multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: Applies an equation-of-motion approach to obtain exact quantum master equations for the extended Jaynes-Cummings model, focusing on population dynamics with double excitations.
result: Successfully derives exact master equations and analyzes double-excitation dynamics, demonstrating the method's applicability to complex dissipative systems.
conclusion: The equation-of-motion approach is effective for deriving exact master equations in multistate cavity QED systems, enabling detailed study of quantum dissipative dynamics.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, and Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the Maximum Independent Set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The Maximum Independent Set problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embeddings require large atom overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to embed arbitrary graphs, leveraging the van der Waals interaction to encode the MIS constraint with fewer atoms.
result: The 3D embedding scheme achieves a polynomial reduction in atom count compared to 2D embeddings, enabling the solution of larger MIS instances.
conclusion: This work advances the practical implementation of quantum optimization on Rydberg platforms by improving resource efficiency.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the detection loophole affects the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria, finding that the PPT criterion's advantage diminishes under realistic conditions.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world detectors have inefficiencies (detection loophole) that can compromise the reliability of detection methods. The paper aims to compare the robustness of two key criteria under such practical constraints.
method: The authors analyze the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria in the presence of a detection loophole, using theoretical models and numerical simulations to evaluate their detection capabilities.
result: While the PPT criterion outperforms moment-based criteria in ideal setups, its advantage is significantly reduced when the detection loophole is considered, and in some regimes moment-based criteria become more effective.
conclusion: The detection loophole must be accounted for when choosing entanglement detection methods, and moment-based criteria may be preferable in practical scenarios with detector inefficiencies.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, and Da Zhang

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system via spontaneous four-wave mixing.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are essential for quantum information protocols, but generating energy-time-entangled triphotons with high efficiency and low noise remains challenging.
method: A six-level cold atomic system is used to realize spontaneous four-wave mixing, producing energy-time-entangled triphotons with controlled nonlinear susceptibility.
result: The scheme generates energy-time-entangled triphotons with improved efficiency and reduced noise compared to previous hot atomic ensemble approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for generating multiphoton entanglement, which can be used in quantum networks and quantum communication protocols.

title: Revealing Emergent Many-body Phenomena By Analyzing Large-scale Space-time Records Of Monitored Quantum Systems
authors: Marcel Cech, Cecilia de Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, And Federico Carollo
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Cech, Cecilia De Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, and Federico Carollo

Midcircuit measurements allow the probing of quantum many-body dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution. In this work, the authors discuss how these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060201] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses midcircuit measurements to reveal emergent many-body phenomena in monitored quantum systems, analyzing space-time records.
motivation: Understanding emergent phenomena in quantum many-body systems is crucial, and midcircuit measurements offer a way to probe dynamics with high resolution.
method: The authors analyze large-scale space-time records obtained from monitored quantum systems, likely using numerical simulations or theoretical frameworks.
result: They demonstrate that these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena, such as phase transitions or dynamical patterns.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements are a powerful tool for uncovering emergent behavior in quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in the digital-analog quantum computing paradigm, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a resource-efficient alternative to fully digital gate-based quantum computing, but designing circuits for Hamiltonian simulation remains challenging.
method: The authors derive explicit analytical formulas for simulating target Hamiltonians using the native interaction Hamiltonian of a given platform combined with single-qubit gates.
result: They provide closed-form expressions for the required digital-analog circuit parameters, enabling efficient simulation of a wide class of Hamiltonians.
conclusion: The explicit formulas simplify the implementation of Hamiltonian simulation on digital-analog quantum processors, potentially reducing circuit depth and improving fidelity.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Combines super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial spin interactions.
motivation: Protecting quantum states from noise is crucial for quantum information processing; existing methods like dynamical decoupling may be inefficient for certain types of noise.
method: The protocol uses frequent projective measurements (super-Zeno effect) on carefully chosen anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise from spin interactions of polynomial order.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects against unwanted rotations; for spin-3/2, average fidelity scales as 1 - F̄ ∝ t^4, showing improved protection.
conclusion: The proposed protocol offers a novel way to protect quantum states from specific noise types, with potential applications in quantum memory and metrology.

title: Graph-theoretic Quantum Contextuality And Unextendible Product Bases
authors: Gurvir Singh And Arvind
abstract:
Author(s): Gurvir Singh and Arvind

Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are central to the study of local distinguishability of orthogonal product states. While their connection to quantum nonlocality via Bell inequalities is well established, their link to quantum contextuality remains largely unexplored. We establish a graph theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062409] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a graph-theoretic connection between quantum contextuality and unextendible product bases (UPBs).
motivation: UPBs are known for nonlocality but their link to contextuality was unexplored; the paper aims to fill this gap.
method: Uses graph theory to represent UPBs and derive contextuality inequalities from the graph's properties.
result: Shows that certain UPBs exhibit contextuality, providing a new perspective on the structure of UPBs.
conclusion: The graph-theoretic approach reveals a deeper connection between contextuality and UPBs, with implications for quantum foundations and information.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery between two QEC codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates are essential for universal quantum computing but typically require costly magic state distillation; this work aims to reduce overhead.
method: Generalized lattice surgery is used to integrate two quantum error-correcting codes, enabling logical non-Clifford gates without distillation.
result: The scheme completes the universal gate set in a fault-tolerant manner while avoiding distillation overhead.
conclusion: This approach offers a more efficient path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Ergodicity And Hydrodynamics: From Quantum To Classical Spin Systems
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, And Leonardo Mazza
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, and Leonardo Mazza

We show that in classical spin systems, the precise nature of the late-time hydrodynamic tails of the autocorrelation functions of a generic observable is determined by (i) the dynamical critical exponent and (ii) the equilibrium thermodynamic properties of the corresponding observable. We provide n…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064102] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that late-time hydrodynamic tails in classical spin systems are determined by dynamical critical exponent and equilibrium thermodynamic properties, with a quantum extension.
motivation: Understanding the late-time behavior of correlation functions in spin systems is fundamental to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and hydrodynamics.
method: The authors derive general relations connecting hydrodynamic tails to thermodynamic susceptibilities and dynamical critical exponent, and extend the analysis to quantum systems using linear response theory.
result: They provide explicit formulas for the asymptotic decay of autocorrelation functions in both classical and quantum spin systems, validated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work unifies the description of hydrodynamic tails across classical and quantum regimes, highlighting the role of equilibrium thermodynamics in non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Complexity-powered Machine Intelligent Classification Of Quantum Many-body Dynamics
authors: Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), And Jie Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), and Jie Ren (任捷)

Identifying and classifying quantum phases from measurable time series in many-body dynamics have significant values, yet lack details and face formidable challenges, requiring the profound knowledge of physicists. Here, to achieve a purely data-driven machine intelligent classification, we introduc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Uses machine learning on time series complexity measures to classify quantum many-body phases and dynamics.
motivation: Classifying quantum phases from dynamics is challenging; a data-driven method could bypass the need for deep physical insight.
method: Introduces a complexity measure based on time series analysis and applies machine learning to classify phases from simulated dynamics.
result: Demonstrates that complexity-powered machine learning can accurately classify different quantum many-body phases.
conclusion: The approach offers a purely data-driven way to identify quantum phases, potentially useful for experimental data.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between local and global quantum resources is fundamental for quantum information processing. This work aims to experimentally verify a theoretical bound on the sum of local coherence and quantum mutual information.
method: The authors prepare two-qubit states and measure local coherence (via l1 norm of coherence) and quantum mutual information. They vary the state parameters to explore the trade-off and compare with the theoretical upper bound.
result: The sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit, confirming the predicted complementarity relation.
conclusion: The results provide experimental evidence for a fundamental trade-off between local and global quantum resources, which may have implications for quantum information tasks and resource theories.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond via optical spectroscopy, focusing on linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phonon interactions in color centers is crucial for improving coherence and performance in quantum networking and sensing applications.
method: Optical probing techniques, including linewidth analysis and coherent population trapping measurements, are used to characterize the phononic environment of SnV centers.
result: The study reveals phonon-induced linewidth broadening and demonstrates coherent population trapping between ground-state orbital levels, providing insights into the phononic properties.
conclusion: The findings contribute to optimizing SnV centers as quantum emitters for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication requires accounting for relativistic effects due to high altitudes and velocities, which can affect the security and performance of CV-QKD.
method: The authors systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse Doppler, and gravitational contributions, and model their impact on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how these shifts degrade the secret key rate and provide corrections to maintain security.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be considered in satellite CV-QKD to ensure reliable key distribution, and the proposed corrections enable practical implementation.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that allows for consistent treatment of pathwise observables across both jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in systems with discrete jumps, advancing non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, multi-component condensates, and analogies to neural networks and thermodynamic computing.
result: They argue that condensates can implement classification, sensing, and memory via composition and phase behavior, with potential for energy-efficient computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a new paradigm for information processing in biology, with implications for synthetic biology and unconventional computing.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands under high magnetic fields.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower equilibration with nuclear spins.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs the heating dynamics, providing insights into thermalization in low-dimensional systems.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations from single-shot measurements, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, which can aid in understanding decoherence and improving qubit performance.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction codes must be tailored.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are demonstrated, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from random matrix theory and statistical physics, deriving bounds on the variance of the loss function and its dependence on circuit depth, noise rate, and expressivity.
result: They find that noise can actually help concentration by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to a trade-off between noise and trainability. Explicit formulas for the loss function variance are provided.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise and circuit structure, potentially improving the training of variational algorithms.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics, but the regime where strings exhibit complex quantum dynamics is not well explored.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, likely tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study string-breaking dynamics in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking is not instantaneous but shows rich quantum dynamics, including oscillations and multi-particle production.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for quantum simulators to observe non-equilibrium phenomena in confining systems, bridging quantum thermodynamics and many-body dynamics.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without extra overhead, preserving key code parameters and enabling more efficient quantum computation.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing a resource-efficient method for parallel logical measurements.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo
