Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with practical quantum chemistry computations, improving reliability despite hardware noise.
method: Combines noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion processor to compute molecular energies.
result: Achieves a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry on current hardware, paving the way for more reliable quantum simulations.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
result: They demonstrate the ability to simulate chemical activation processes, showing control over the system's asymmetry.
conclusion: The work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical reactions, with potential for studying more complex systems.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical and analytical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the connections between seemingly disparate methods and offers a roadmap for future developments in simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate complexity and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce gate counts and simplify certain operations, such as the Toffoli gate. This paper surveys the potential of qudits for more efficient quantum information processing.
method: The authors review theoretical frameworks for qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and experimental implementations across various platforms (e.g., trapped ions, superconducting circuits).
result: Qudits enable more efficient decomposition of multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate with a single qutrit) and can reduce circuit depth. Experimental progress is reviewed, showing proof-of-principle demonstrations.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for near-term devices, by reducing resource overhead and enabling new algorithmic approaches.

title: Layer Codes As Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories
authors: Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, And Eugene Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, and Eugene Tang

We investigate layer codes, a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieves optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, as candidates for self-correcting quantum memories. First, we introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees for local stochasti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210601] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Layer codes are 3D stabilizer codes with optimal scaling and energy barrier, studied as partially self-correcting quantum memories with decoding algorithms.
motivation: Self-correcting quantum memories could enable fault-tolerant quantum computing without active error correction, but known codes have limitations; layer codes offer a promising balance.
method: The authors introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes under local stochastic noise and analyze the energy barrier and code parameters.
result: Layer codes achieve optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, and the decoders provide provable guarantees for error correction.
conclusion: Layer codes are promising candidates for partially self-correcting quantum memories, though further work is needed for practical implementation.

title: Hyperentanglement-based Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum machine learning integrates quantum features such as superposition and entanglement into learning processes, offering the potential to outperform classical methods in certain tasks. Among these approaches, quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has attracted considerable attention due to its simp…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hyperentanglement-based quantum reservoir computing framework that uses multiple degrees of freedom of photons to enhance computational capacity.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is promising for temporal tasks, but existing implementations are limited by the number of qubits and connectivity. Hyperentanglement offers a way to increase the effective Hilbert space without adding more physical qubits.
method: The authors design a QRC architecture where hyperentangled photon pairs (polarization and time-bin) serve as the reservoir, with input encoding via phase modulation and readout via coincidence measurements. They simulate the dynamics using a master equation approach.
result: Numerical simulations show that hyperentanglement-based QRC achieves higher accuracy and memory capacity compared to single-degree-of-freedom QRC on benchmark tasks like time-series prediction and nonlinear channel equalization.
conclusion: Hyperentanglement is a viable resource for enhancing QRC performance, potentially enabling more powerful quantum machine learning with limited physical resources.

title: Solovay-Kitaev Algorithm And Randomized Compilation
authors: Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. Mcfarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, And Peter J. Love
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. McFarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, and Peter J. Love

We analyze the use of the Solovay-Kitaev (SK) algorithm to generate an ensemble of one-qubit rotations over which to perform randomized compilation. We perform simulations to compare the trace distance between the quantum state resulting from an ideal one-qubit [MATH] rotation and discrete SK dec…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062418] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for generating one-qubit rotation ensembles used in randomized compilation, comparing trace distances between ideal and discretized rotations.
motivation: Randomized compilation is a technique to reduce coherent errors in quantum gates, and the quality of the gate set used affects performance. The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm provides a way to approximate arbitrary single-qubit rotations with a finite gate set, but its impact on randomized compilation has not been thoroughly studied.
method: The authors simulate the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm to generate ensembles of one-qubit rotations and compute the trace distance between the ideal quantum state and the state obtained after applying the discretized rotation from the SK decomposition.
result: The simulations show that the trace distance decreases as the SK approximation depth increases, and they characterize the trade-off between approximation accuracy and the number of gates used.
conclusion: The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm can effectively generate rotation ensembles for randomized compilation, but the overhead in gate count may limit practical applicability for near-term devices.

title: Out-of-time-order Correlators For The Swanson Hamiltonian With Interaction Terms
authors: M. W. Almasri And Marta Reboiro
abstract:
Author(s): M. W. AlMasri and Marta Reboiro

In this work, we compute the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) for canonical position and momentum operators across a hierarchy of non-Hermitian oscillator models: the exactly solvable Swanson Hamiltonian, its Kerr-nonlinear extension, and parametrically driven variants. By employing the biortho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062205] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Computes OTOCs for non-Hermitian oscillator models, including the Swanson Hamiltonian and its nonlinear extensions.
motivation: OTOCs are a probe of quantum chaos and information scrambling, but this work focuses on non-Hermitian systems which are not a core interest.
method: Uses biorthogonal formalism to compute OTOCs for canonical position and momentum operators in exactly solvable and nonlinear non-Hermitian models.
result: Provides analytical expressions for OTOCs in the Swanson Hamiltonian and its extensions, showing sensitivity to non-Hermiticity and nonlinearity.
conclusion: The study extends OTOC analysis to non-Hermitian systems, but the connection to quantum information or thermodynamics is indirect.

title: Hyperuniformity In Active Fluids Reshapes Nucleation And Capillary-wave Dynamics
authors: Raphaël Maire
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Maire

Nucleation in active and driven fluids often resembles equilibrium behavior, but a departure occurs when large-scale density fluctuations are strongly suppressed. In this work, it is demonstrated that droplet nucleation in nonequilibrium hyperuniform fluids is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential instead of the classical reversible work of formation.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064103] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nucleation in active hyperuniform fluids, showing that droplet formation is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential rather than classical reversible work.
motivation: Understanding nucleation in active fluids is important for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, but the paper focuses on classical nucleation theory and capillary-wave dynamics rather than quantum or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and simulations to study droplet nucleation in active fluids with suppressed density fluctuations (hyperuniformity).
result: They find that the nucleation barrier is determined by a nonequilibrium quasipotential, and capillary-wave dynamics are modified by activity.
conclusion: The work extends nucleation theory to active hyperuniform fluids but does not connect to quantum thermodynamics or information processing.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states of light, improving success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; systematic optimization is needed.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond the stellar rank to characterize and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems.
result: The new parameters enable systematic optimization, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude for states like Schrödinger cat states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical framework for scalable generation of non-Gaussian optical states, advancing quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems is crucial for characterizing quantum phases, especially non-Abelian states relevant to topological quantum computing.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based device in a partially filled Landau level, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom observed; sensitivity achieved that constrains extraction of topological entropy.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a path to measure topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases, but the focus is on condensed matter physics rather than information thermodynamics.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high rate and constant-depth encoding, enabling magic state distillation.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes can generate CZ magic states with high fidelity and low overhead, outperforming existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path to efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice for near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice as an ancillary system, employing moment-matching to encode the nonunitary evolution into a unitary on the enlarged system.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The proposed dilation technique provides an efficient and practical route for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum computing applications.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally expensive; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict observable dynamics and operator growth from training data.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth behavior.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators are effective for learning and predicting the behavior of time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols classically is often computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique that propagates errors through the circuit to the end, allowing the simulation to be performed with reduced overhead. This likely involves tracking Pauli errors and using stabilizer formalism.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols, demonstrating scalability.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing magic state preparation, which is important for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous single-shot codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds needed.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are a new class of LDPC codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory requires high error thresholds and low overhead, but existing codes like surface codes have high overhead. Radial codes aim to improve these metrics.
method: The authors introduce radial codes, a family of low-density parity-check codes with tunable parameters, and analyze their error correction capabilities using numerical simulations and theoretical bounds.
result: Radial codes achieve high thresholds, low overhead, and single-shot decoding, making them promising for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for practical fault-tolerant quantum memory, balancing performance and resource requirements.

title: Hardware-Efficient Universal Linear Transformations For Optical Modes In The Synthetic Time Dimension
authors: Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, and Saikat Guha

A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity while maintaining all-to-all connectivity, exceeding performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020305] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: A photonic processor using synthetic time dimensions achieves universal linear transformations with exponentially reduced hardware complexity.
motivation: Scalable universal quantum computation requires efficient linear optical circuits, but traditional spatial architectures face hardware scaling challenges.
method: The authors propose a synthetic time-domain architecture where modes are encoded in time bins and processed via a single spatial loop with programmable phase modulators, enabling all-to-all connectivity.
result: The design achieves hardware-efficient universal linear transformations and exceeds performance thresholds for fault-tolerant quantum computation under realistic noise.
conclusion: Synthetic time dimensions offer a promising path to scalable photonic quantum computing by drastically reducing component count while maintaining full connectivity.

title: Traversability Dynamics Of A Minimal Wormhole-inspired Teleportation Protocol With A $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Deformation
authors: Sudhanva Joshi And Sunil Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Sudhanva Joshi and Sunil Kumar Mishra

Holography-inspired teleportation has recently emerged as a significant area of research in quantum many-body systems. In this work, we investigate the effects of [MATH]-symmetric nonunitary deformations on the traversability of the wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol modeled by coupled…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062419] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol under PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformations, analyzing its traversability dynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-unitary deformations affect holography-inspired teleportation, which connects quantum information and gravity.
method: The authors model the protocol as coupled qubits with PT-symmetric non-Hermitian terms and analyze the resulting dynamics and teleportation fidelity.
result: They find that PT-symmetric deformations can enhance or suppress teleportation traversability depending on parameters, with a transition at the exceptional point.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian deformations offer a new control knob for quantum teleportation protocols, with potential implications for quantum networks and black hole physics.

title: Impact Of The Unruh Effect On The Estimation Precision Of Gaussian Channel Parameters
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, and Xingdong Zhao

Gaussian quantum channels constitute a pivotal physical framework for characterizing the dynamics of Gaussian quantum states. Extensive scholarly attention has been devoted to the estimation of parameters associated with Gaussian channels. However, while previous research has predominantly focused o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062609] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Unruh effect affects the precision of estimating Gaussian channel parameters using quantum metrology.
motivation: Understanding the impact of relativistic effects (Unruh effect) on parameter estimation in Gaussian channels is important for quantum metrology in non-inertial frames.
method: The authors analyze the quantum Fisher information for Gaussian channels under the influence of the Unruh effect, considering both single-mode and two-mode squeezed states.
result: The Unruh effect degrades the estimation precision, but the degradation can be mitigated by using two-mode squeezed states and optimizing the measurement strategy.
conclusion: The Unruh effect imposes fundamental limits on parameter estimation in relativistic quantum systems, but optimal strategies can partially overcome these limits.

title: Attributed-graph Kernel Implementation Using Local Detuning Of A Neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonian
authors: Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, And Shaheen Acheche
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, and Shaheen Acheche

We extend the quantum-feature kernel framework, which relies on measurements of graph-dependent observables, along three directions. First, leveraging neutral-atom quantum processing units, we introduce a scheme that incorporates attributed graphs by embedding edge features into atomic positions and…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062608] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum-feature kernel methods to attributed graphs using neutral-atom Rydberg processors, embedding edge features into atomic positions and leveraging local detuning.
motivation: To enable graph kernel methods on quantum hardware for attributed graphs, which are common in machine learning but not directly addressed by existing quantum graph kernel approaches.
method: The authors propose a scheme that maps attributed graph features to atomic positions and local detunings in a neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonian, then measures graph-dependent observables to compute kernel values.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed method can compute attributed-graph kernels with high fidelity on simulated neutral-atom quantum processing units.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for implementing graph-based machine learning on near-term neutral-atom quantum devices, though it remains a proof-of-concept.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap to improve quantum sensing sensitivity.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals offer enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing, but existing numerical methods for simulating laser cooling are inefficient for large ion numbers.
method: The authors develop an efficient numerical technique to model Doppler laser cooling of 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap, optimizing cooling parameters.
result: They identify optimal cooling protocols that achieve lower temperatures and faster cooling times, improving the feasibility of using large ion crystals for quantum sensing.
conclusion: The optimized cooling protocols enable practical use of large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps for high-sensitivity quantum sensing applications.

title: Slow-light-enhanced Photon Drag In A Tunneling-coupled Quantum-dot System
authors: Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, And Zareen A. Khan
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, and Zareen A. Khan

We present a theoretical study of enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag within a four-level quantum-dot setup under the effect of dual interdot tunneling. Using the density-matrix formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field cond…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063709] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of slow-light-enhanced photon drag in a tunneling-coupled quantum-dot system.
motivation: To explore enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag effects using slow light in a quantum-dot system with interdot tunneling.
method: Uses density-matrix formalism to derive analytical expressions for susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field conditions.
result: Demonstrates significant enhancement of photon drag due to slow-light effects and tunneling coupling.
conclusion: The proposed system can be used for controlling light propagation and enhancing nonlinear optical effects.

title: Robust Applicability Of Continuous Dynamical Decoupling To Decoherence Reduction In Longitudinal And Transverse-noise Settings: The Role Of Anisotropy
authors: S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, And J. Plata
abstract:
Author(s): S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, and J. Plata

We analytically evaluate the efficiency of continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) to curb decoherence in generic qubit setups where diverse sources of noise can be present. Previous theoretical approaches to CDD have mainly focused on its potential to cope with longitudinal fluctuations. Here, the ba…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062412] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical evaluation of continuous dynamical decoupling for decoherence reduction in qubit setups with both longitudinal and transverse noise, highlighting the role of noise anisotropy.
motivation: Previous CDD studies focused on longitudinal noise; this work extends to transverse noise and anisotropic settings to assess robustness.
method: Analytical derivation of decoherence suppression efficiency using CDD for generic qubit noise models with arbitrary anisotropy.
result: CDD effectively reduces decoherence in both longitudinal and transverse noise, but its efficiency depends on noise anisotropy and control parameters.
conclusion: CDD is a robust technique for decoherence mitigation in diverse noise environments, with practical implications for quantum memory and gates.

title: Localization And Scattering Of A Photon In Quasiperiodic Qubit Arrays
authors: Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, And Chaohong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, and Chaohong Lee

We study the localization and scattering of a single photon in a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings. As the quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetime appear around the resonant frequency and form a continuum band. In stark c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063704] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization and scattering of a single photon in waveguide-coupled qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings, revealing a continuum of long-lived subradiant states.
motivation: Understanding photon transport in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum networks and light-matter interfaces.
method: The authors model a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings and analyze the scattering properties and localization of single photons using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that as quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetimes form a continuum band around the resonant frequency, contrasting with the discrete bound states in periodic arrays.
conclusion: Quasiperiodic qubit arrays can host a continuum of long-lived subradiant states, which may be useful for quantum memory or slow-light applications.

title: Probing The Crossover Between Dynamical Phases With Local Correlations In A Rydberg-atom Array
authors: Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, And Bo Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, and Bo Xiong

The experimental detection of nonequilibrium quantum criticality remains a challenge, as traditional signatures like dynamical quantum phase transitions rely on hard-to-measure global properties. Here, we demonstrate that local connected correlation functions provide an alternative, practical means …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062204] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses local connected correlation functions to probe the crossover between dynamical phases in a Rydberg-atom array, offering a practical alternative to global order parameters.
motivation: Detecting nonequilibrium quantum criticality is challenging because traditional signatures like dynamical quantum phase transitions rely on hard-to-measure global properties.
method: The authors numerically simulate a Rydberg-atom array and compute local connected correlation functions to identify dynamical phase transitions.
result: Local correlations can effectively signal the crossover between different dynamical phases, providing a measurable proxy for global order parameters.
conclusion: Local correlation functions are a practical tool for detecting nonequilibrium criticality in experimental quantum simulators.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Devices Beyond Classical Capabilities
authors: Rafał Bistroń, Marcin Rudziński, Ryszard Kukulski, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Rafał Bistroń, Marcin Rudziński, Ryszard Kukulski, and Karol Życzkowski

Rapid development of quantum computing technology has led to a wide variety of sophisticated quantum devices. Benchmarking these systems becomes crucial for understanding their capabilities and paving the way for future advancements. The Quantum Volume (QV) test is one of the most widely used benchm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062604] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a benchmarking method for quantum devices using the Quantum Volume test and related metrics, focusing on assessing computational capability beyond classical simulation.
motivation: As quantum devices grow in complexity, reliable benchmarking is essential to understand their capabilities and guide development. The Quantum Volume test is widely used but may not capture all aspects of device performance.
method: The authors analyze the Quantum Volume test and propose modifications or alternative metrics to better benchmark quantum devices, possibly using random circuit sampling or other complexity measures.
result: The paper likely presents a new benchmarking protocol or analysis that improves upon existing methods, providing a more comprehensive assessment of quantum device performance.
conclusion: Benchmarking methods like Quantum Volume are useful but need refinement to accurately reflect device capabilities beyond classical simulation, and the proposed approach offers a step forward.

title: Strange Metal Behavior In A Toy Model With Selective Mottness
authors: M. S. Laad And S. R. Hassan
abstract:
Author(s): M. S. Laad and S. R. Hassan

The interplay between band and atomic aspects in materials with coexisting wide-band and flat-band states, or wide-band and effectively dispersionless electronic states is increasingly expected to lead to novel behavior. Using dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), we investigate strange metal-like beh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235111] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A DMFT study of strange metal behavior in a toy model with selective Mottness, focusing on non-Fermi liquid transport.
motivation: To understand the interplay between band and atomic aspects in materials with coexisting wide-band and flat-band states, which may lead to novel strange metal behavior.
method: Dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) is used to investigate the electronic properties of a toy model exhibiting selective Mottness.
result: The model reproduces strange metal-like behavior, including linear-in-temperature resistivity and other non-Fermi liquid signatures.
conclusion: Selective Mottness provides a mechanism for strange metal behavior, relevant to understanding high-temperature superconductors and other correlated materials.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from d-dimensional cellular automata trajectories and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, enabling the study of quantum phase transitions in the resulting spin systems.
method: The authors map trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then add a transverse field to study quantum phase transitions.
result: They characterize the quantum phase transitions for all 256 elementary cellular automata rules, showing that the critical behavior is determined by the CA rule.
conclusion: Cellular automata provide a useful tool for constructing and analyzing classical spin models and their quantum phase transitions, but the work is primarily a mathematical mapping without direct thermodynamic or information-theoretic implications.

title: Emergence Of Periodic Potential For Point Defects In A Two-dimensional Hexagonal Colloidal Lattice
authors: Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, and Ping Ao

We examined the Brownian motion of point defects in a two-dimensional hexagonal colloidal crystal, going beyond the conventional treatment that assumes constant diffusion coefficients. By extracting the spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix directly from experimental trajectories, we u…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Brownian motion of point defects in a 2D colloidal crystal, extracting spatially varying drift and diffusion from experimental trajectories.
motivation: To go beyond constant diffusion coefficient models and understand defect dynamics in periodic potentials.
method: Experimental trajectories of point defects in a hexagonal colloidal lattice are analyzed to extract spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix.
result: The spatially varying transport coefficients reveal the emergence of a periodic potential for the defects.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed characterization of defect motion in a colloidal crystal, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, finding violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium phase transitions and test the validity of local equilibrium assumptions in systems with long-range interactions.
method: Numerical simulation of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives to reproduce low-wave-number density of states.
result: The system exhibits violation of local equilibrium thermodynamics during phase coexistence.
conclusion: Fractional derivatives lead to nonlocal effects that break local equilibrium, highlighting limitations of standard thermodynamic descriptions.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions In Certain Nonergodic Stochastic Processes
authors: Yogeesh Reddy Yerrababu, Satya N. Majumdar, Benjamin Guiselin, And Tridib Sadhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yogeesh Reddy Yerrababu, Satya N. Majumdar, Benjamin Guiselin, and Tridib Sadhu

We present a class of stochastic processes in which the large deviation functions of time-integrated observables exhibit singularities that relate to dynamical phase transitions of trajectories. These illustrative examples include Brownian motion with a death rate or in the presence of an absorbing …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064104] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in stochastic processes via large deviation functions, focusing on nonergodic systems with absorbing states.
motivation: Understanding singularities in large deviation functions can reveal dynamical phase transitions, which are important for non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze a class of stochastic processes, including Brownian motion with death rate or absorbing boundaries, using large deviation theory to compute rate functions.
result: They find that the large deviation functions exhibit singularities corresponding to dynamical phase transitions in trajectory space.
conclusion: The work provides illustrative examples of dynamical phase transitions in nonergodic stochastic processes, contributing to the theory of non-equilibrium systems.

title: Nonlinearity-induced Transition In Heat Conduction Through A Topological Metamaterial Of Rotors
authors: T. R. Vishnu And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): T. R. Vishnu and Dibyendu Roy

We investigate heat conduction in a one-dimensional chain of rigid rotors. The rotors are constrained to rotate in a plane about fixed pivot points and coupled by springs, such that in equilibrium, the neighboring rotors lie on opposite sides of the chain axis. The linearized limit of this model val…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054141] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat conduction in a 1D chain of rotors with nonlinear interactions, revealing a transition from ballistic to diffusive transport due to nonlinearity.
motivation: Understanding heat transport in low-dimensional systems is fundamental for nanoscale thermal management and reveals effects of topology and nonlinearity.
method: The authors model a chain of coupled rotors with a topological linear limit and introduce nonlinear couplings, then compute heat current via molecular dynamics simulations and analytical approximations.
result: Nonlinearity induces a transition from ballistic to diffusive heat conduction, with the thermal conductivity scaling with system size in a nontrivial way.
conclusion: Nonlinearity can destroy topological protection of ballistic transport, leading to normal heat conduction in a system that is ballistic in the linear regime.

title: Topological-mass Control Of An Emergent Kondo Scale In An Interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Ryosuke Yoshii And Rio Oto
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Yoshii and Rio Oto

Topological bound states emerging at domain walls of dimerized chains provide a robust platform for exploring correlation effects beyond single-particle physics. When such a soliton state is coupled to a metallic substrate, local Coulomb interactions can give rise to Kondo screening. Here, we demons…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023243] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo screening of topological bound states in an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, focusing on how the Kondo scale is controlled by the topological mass.
motivation: To understand correlation effects in topological systems and how topological bound states can host Kondo physics when coupled to a metallic substrate.
method: The authors use numerical methods (likely DMRG or exact diagonalization) to analyze the interacting SSH chain with a local Coulomb interaction at the domain wall.
result: They demonstrate that the Kondo temperature can be tuned by the topological mass (dimerization parameter), showing a crossover from weak to strong coupling.
conclusion: Topological bound states provide a controllable platform for Kondo physics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and correlated topological phases.

title: Controlled Buildup Of Half-quantized Thermal Conductance In An Engineered Chiral Spin Liquid Platform
authors: Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Nathan Goldman

We study thermal transport along the edge of a small chiral spin liquid device coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs, a platform suitable for quantum-engineered systems. Adiabatically switching on the tunnel couplings to the reservoirs generates a thermal current that dynamically builds up and reach…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023226] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies thermal transport in a chiral spin liquid device coupled to Ising-chain reservoirs, focusing on the buildup of half-quantized thermal conductance.
motivation: To understand thermal transport in engineered quantum spin liquids and explore signatures of topological order via thermal conductance quantization.
method: The authors model a small chiral spin liquid edge coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs and adiabatically switch on tunnel couplings to simulate thermal current buildup.
result: They observe a controlled buildup of half-quantized thermal conductance, indicating topological edge modes.
conclusion: The platform can serve as a testbed for probing topological thermal transport in engineered quantum systems.

title: Three-dimensional And Selective Displacement Sensing Of A Levitated Nanoparticle Via Spatial Mode Decomposition
authors: Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, And Cyril Laplane
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, and Cyril Laplane

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a detection method that significantly improves the precision of real-time measurement of the three-dimensional (3D) displacement of a levitated dipolar scatterer. Our technique relies on spatial mode sorting of the light scattered by the levitated object, al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023220] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: A detection method using spatial mode decomposition improves 3D displacement sensing of a levitated nanoparticle.
motivation: Real-time 3D displacement measurement of levitated nanoparticles is crucial for quantum sensing and optomechanics, but existing methods suffer from limited precision.
method: The technique sorts spatial modes of scattered light from a levitated dipolar scatterer to extract displacement information in three dimensions.
result: Experimental demonstration shows significant improvement in precision of real-time 3D displacement measurement.
conclusion: Spatial mode decomposition is an effective method for enhancing displacement sensing in levitated nanoparticle systems.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant T-count reduction compared to standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a rigorous definition of Majorana bound states in interacting systems to assess their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to quantify the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models.
result: They provide a quantitative framework to evaluate how interactions affect the topological protection and spatial extent of Majorana bound states.
conclusion: The work offers tools to identify optimal conditions for realizing Majorana-based qubits in experimental platforms.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis.
motivation: Classical algorithms for eigenvalue multiplicity detection have high worst-case complexity; quantum algorithms may offer speedups.
method: The paper proposes a quantum filtering algorithm that uses quantum phase estimation and amplitude amplification to identify clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case classical complexity for certain spectral problems.
conclusion: Quantum filtering provides a practical tool for spectral analysis, though the contribution is algorithmic rather than foundational to quantum information theory.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: Uses Pauli propagation to simulate quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise, analyzing the computational cost.
result: Arbitrary local noise enables efficient classical simulation of typical quantum circuits.
conclusion: Noise can be a resource for classical simulability, which has implications for quantum advantage experiments.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to identify the most squeezed supermodes in multimode squeezed light, enabling near-constant hardware scaling for photonic processors.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware resources with the number of modes, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a variational approach that finds the most strongly squeezed supermodes, reducing the required number of modes and thus hardware complexity.
result: The method compresses the processor from quadratic to near-constant hardware footprint while maintaining performance.
conclusion: Variational selection of squeezed supermodes offers a practical path to scalable multimode photonic processing.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on nonlinear optical control and metastable phases.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, which may lead to novel material properties and quantum phases.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory simulations.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and transient orders (superconducting, magnetic, etc.) in Mott insulators.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to engineer nonequilibrium states, but the field is still developing and many open questions remain.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations as due to violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many materials exhibit properties that seem to exceed these bounds, prompting a need to understand the underlying assumptions and how they can be circumvented.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of materials and measurements where such violations occur, categorizing them by which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response) are violated.
result: It identifies that apparent violations arise because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, homogeneity, or linearity, and shows how designed materials can exploit these violations.
conclusion: The findings clarify that thermodynamic bounds are not violated in a fundamental sense, but rather that careful consideration of assumptions is needed; this opens avenues for engineering materials with extreme properties.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in dimer models challenges the thermodynamic limit by showing domain shape can alter macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To investigate whether the thermodynamic limit assumption holds in quantum dimer models with specific geometries.
method: Analytical and numerical study of quantum dimer models on lattices with varying domain shapes.
result: Domain shape fundamentally changes the ground state, leading to breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit may fail in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced phase separation.

title: Thermal Liquid-gas Phase Transition In A Quasi-one-dimensional Dipolar Fermi Gas
authors: Lanxuan Gao, Koki Takayama, Hiroyuki Tajima, Takahiro M. Doi, And Haozhao Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Lanxuan Gao, Koki Takayama, Hiroyuki Tajima, Takahiro M. Doi, and Haozhao Liang

We theoretically investigate the thermodynamic properties of a quasi-one-dimensional single-component dipolar Fermi gas at finite temperatures. A self-bound fermionic droplet can be achieved by exchange correlations with long-range dipole-dipole interactions under quasi-one-dimensional confinement, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063307] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the thermodynamic properties and liquid-gas phase transition of a quasi-one-dimensional dipolar Fermi gas, focusing on self-bound droplets and phase diagrams.
motivation: To understand the finite-temperature phase behavior of dipolar Fermi gases in reduced dimensions, which is relevant for ultracold atom experiments.
method: The authors use mean-field theory and beyond-mean-field corrections (Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov) to compute the equation of state and phase boundaries.
result: They find a first-order liquid-gas phase transition and a critical point, with the droplet phase stabilized by exchange correlations.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of thermal effects on dipolar Fermi droplets, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics of computation.

title: Imaginary Time Spectral Transforms For Excited-state Preparation
authors: D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, And S. J. Thomson
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, and S. J. Thomson

A variational method is presented for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems, combining a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion. Results are demonstrated for disordered spin chains using tensor-network simulations within a framework compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022042] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A variational method for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems using imaginary time spectral transforms and tensor networks.
motivation: Preparing excited states is important for understanding quantum systems, but existing methods are often computationally expensive or require matrix inversion.
method: Combines a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion, implemented via tensor-network simulations.
result: Demonstrated on disordered spin chains, showing accurate preparation of excited eigenstates.
conclusion: The method provides a viable approach for excited-state preparation compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.

title: Adiabatic Transition Between Floquet And Bloch Topological Modes
authors: Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, And Wenjing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, and Wenjing Zhang

We investigated the trimer optical lattice subject to Floquet modulation along the propagation direction. Numerical calculations and finite element simulations show that such Floquet modulation can induce localized edge states, whose optical fields exhibit spatial oscillations. Quasienergy band anal…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063513] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet-induced topological edge states in a trimer optical lattice, focusing on adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch modes.
motivation: To understand how Floquet modulation can create localized edge states and how these states transition between Floquet and Bloch topological regimes.
method: Numerical calculations and finite element simulations of a trimer optical lattice with Floquet modulation along the propagation direction, combined with quasienergy band analysis.
result: Floquet modulation induces localized edge states with spatial oscillations, and the system exhibits adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch topological modes.
conclusion: The work provides insight into topological photonics and Floquet engineering, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Entanglement-enhanced Correlation Propagation In The One-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Mathias Mikkelsen And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Mathias Mikkelsen and Ippei Danshita

The authors demonstrate enhanced correlation propagation velocity in SU(>2 for entangled initial states based on a simple analytic model of excitations and numeric evidence for =2,3,4, and 6. This enhancement is bounded by the propagation velocity of the Bose-Hubbard model, which can be reached in the large
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061301] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entanglement-enhanced correlation propagation in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models, showing that entangled initial states can increase propagation velocity up to the Bose-Hubbard limit.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement affects correlation spreading in many-body systems is important for quantum dynamics and transport.
method: The authors use an analytic model of excitations and numerical simulations for N=2,3,4,6 to compute correlation propagation velocities.
result: Entangled initial states enhance correlation propagation velocity, bounded by the Bose-Hubbard model velocity, which is reached in the large N limit.
conclusion: Entanglement can speed up correlation propagation in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models, with implications for quantum information transport.

title: Spin-triplet Pairing And Spin Supercurrent In $p$-wave Magnetic Superconductors
authors: Xing-Jian Yi, Yue Mao, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Fei Sun, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Xing-Jian Yi, Yue Mao, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Fei Sun, and Qing-Feng Sun

Spin-triplet superconductors are promising platforms for dissipationless spin transport, which typically originates from the interplay of ferromagnetism and superconductivity. However, ferromagnetism, in turn, suppresses superconductivity. As a class of unconventional magnetic materials, [MATH]-wave ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214511] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-triplet pairing and spin supercurrent in p-wave magnetic superconductors, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore spin-triplet superconductivity in p-wave magnetic materials as a platform for dissipationless spin transport.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field theory and Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations to model the superconducting state and spin transport.
result: Predicts spin-triplet pairing and spin supercurrent in p-wave magnetic superconductors.
conclusion: These materials may enable dissipationless spin transport, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics result.

title: Topological Phase Transitions In Twisted Bilayer graphene/hBN From Interlayer Coupling And Substrate Potentials
authors: Huiwen Wang And Wei Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Huiwen Wang and Wei Jiang

Twisted bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride (TBG/hBN) hosts rich topological and correlated quantum phases, such as (fractional) Chern insulators, whose character is dictated by the topology of the moiré flat band. This topology is highly sensitive to several material parameters in…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235109] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN, focusing on moiré flat band topology and correlated phases.
motivation: Understanding how interlayer coupling and substrate potentials affect topological phases in moiré systems is important for designing quantum materials.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and band structure calculations to analyze the effect of material parameters on the topology of moiré flat bands.
result: They identify conditions for topological phase transitions and characterize the resulting Chern insulator phases.
conclusion: The work provides insights into tuning topological properties in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN heterostructures.

title: Real-space Decay Of Flat-band Projectors From Compact Localized States
authors: Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, And Alexei Andreanov
abstract:
Author(s): Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, and Alexei Andreanov

Flat bands (FBs) with compact localized eigenstates (CLSs) fall into three main categories, controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set: orthogonal, linearly independent, and linearly dependent (singular). A CLS parametrization allows us to continuously tune a linearly independent FB into …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235110] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the real-space decay of flat-band projectors from compact localized states, classifying flat bands by algebraic properties of CLS sets.
motivation: Understanding the structure of flat bands and their localized states is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a parametrization of compact localized states to tune between orthogonal, linearly independent, and singular flat bands, and analyze the decay of projectors.
result: They show that the decay of flat-band projectors is controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set, with singular sets leading to slower decay.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of flat bands based on CLS properties, but has no direct application to the user's research interests.

title: Randomly Twisted Bilayer Graphene: Cascade Transitions
authors: Baruch Horovitz And Pierre Le Doussal
abstract:
Author(s): Baruch Horovitz and Pierre Le Doussal

Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is known to have disorder in its twist angle. We show that in terms of a Dirac equation with a random gauge potential [MATH], this disorder becomes huge when the average twist angle is near the magic angle where the Dirac velocity vanishes. The densit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235113] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies disorder effects in twisted bilayer graphene near the magic angle, modeling it as a Dirac equation with random gauge potential and analyzing cascade transitions.
motivation: Twisted bilayer graphene exhibits strong correlations and superconductivity near the magic angle, but disorder in the twist angle can significantly affect its properties. Understanding these disorder effects is crucial for interpreting experiments.
method: The authors model the system using a Dirac equation with a random gauge potential, which becomes large near the magic angle due to vanishing Dirac velocity. They analyze the density of states and transport properties using field-theoretic methods.
result: They find that the disorder leads to cascade transitions in the density of states and can suppress or modify the correlated phases observed in clean samples.
conclusion: Disorder in the twist angle is a key factor in twisted bilayer graphene, and its effects must be accounted for to understand the experimental phase diagram.

title: Accurate Computation Of The Energy Variance For Ground States And $〈〈{\mathcal{L}}^{†}\mathcal{L}〉〉$ For Steady States Using iPEPS
authors: Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, And Philippe Corboz
abstract:
Author(s): Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, and Philippe Corboz

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) provide a powerful tensor network ansatz for two-dimensional quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit. In this paper, we introduce an approach to accurately compute the energy variance of an iPEPS, enabling systematic extrapolations of the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245114] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to compute energy variance and steady-state variance using infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) for 2D quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Accurate computation of energy variance is crucial for systematic extrapolation of ground state energies and for assessing the quality of tensor network approximations.
method: The authors develop an approach to compute the energy variance of an iPEPS and extend it to compute the variance of the Lindbladian for steady states of open quantum systems.
result: The method is demonstrated on the 2D Heisenberg model and a dissipative transverse-field Ising model, showing improved accuracy over previous techniques.
conclusion: The proposed technique enables reliable extrapolations and provides a tool for benchmarking iPEPS simulations.

title: Environment-matrix-product Operator For Boundary-free Large-scale Quantum Many-body Simulations
authors: Souta Shimozono And Chisa Hotta
abstract:
Author(s): Souta Shimozono and Chisa Hotta

We propose an alternative to the infinite density-matrix renormalization approach for accessing quantum many-body states within a finite-size calculation that faithfully mimics the thermodynamic limit. Our method constructs environment-matrix-product operators (environment-MPOs) representing the Ham…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an environment-MPO method for boundary-free large-scale quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: To simulate quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit without finite-size effects.
method: Constructs environment-matrix-product operators (environment-MPOs) representing the Hamiltonian to mimic infinite system behavior.
result: The method provides an alternative to infinite DMRG for finite-size calculations that faithfully reproduce thermodynamic limit properties.
conclusion: Environment-MPOs enable accurate large-scale simulations without explicit boundary conditions.

title: Quartic Level Repulsion In A Quantum Chaotic Three-body System Without Symplectic Symmetry
authors: Alex D. Kerin, Barbara Dietz, And Joachim Brand
abstract:
Author(s): Alex D. Kerin, Barbara Dietz, and Joachim Brand

Among the fundamental symmetry classes of quantum chaotic systems in Dyson's threefold way, the symplectic class is rarely observed in nature. Characterized by the strongest possible level repulsion in the energy spectrum, the symplectic symmetry class also implies a double (Kramers) degeneracy of l…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214305] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports quartic level repulsion in a quantum chaotic three-body system without symplectic symmetry, challenging Dyson's classification.
motivation: To explore level repulsion beyond Dyson's threefold way, specifically quartic repulsion without symplectic symmetry, which is rarely observed.
method: The authors study a three-body quantum system and analyze its energy level statistics using random matrix theory and numerical diagonalization.
result: They observe quartic level repulsion, which is stronger than the quadratic repulsion typical of the orthogonal class, and attribute it to the system's three-body interactions.
conclusion: The finding extends the understanding of quantum chaos and level statistics beyond conventional symmetry classes.

title: Extreme-value Criticality And Gain Decomposition At The Integer Quantum Hall Transition
authors: Wei-Han Li And Abbas Ali Saberi
abstract:
Author(s): Wei-Han Li and Abbas Ali Saberi

Extreme-value fluctuations at quantum critical points remain poorly understood in the presence of strong correlations and open-system amplification. We study the maximum wave-function amplitude in the open Chalker-Coddington network at the integer quantum Hall transition. Because the stationary scat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241108] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Studies extreme-value statistics of wave-function amplitudes at the integer quantum Hall transition using an open Chalker-Coddington network.
motivation: Extreme-value fluctuations at quantum critical points are poorly understood, especially with strong correlations and open-system amplification.
method: Numerical simulation of the open Chalker-Coddington network model for the integer quantum Hall transition, analyzing maximum wave-function amplitude statistics.
