Numerical simulations of turbulent fluids are paramount to real-life applications, from predicting and modeling flows to diagnostic purposes in engineering. However, they are also computationally challenging due to their intrinsically nonlinear dynamics, which require a very high spatial resolution …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023245] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses tensor train decompositions to compress, simulate, and synthesize turbulent flows, demonstrating computational speedups.
motivation: Turbulent flow simulations are computationally expensive due to high spatial resolution requirements; tensor methods offer a way to reduce complexity.
method: The authors represent turbulent flow data as tensor trains and develop algorithms for compression, simulation, and synthesis using tensor network techniques.
result: They achieve significant compression ratios and speedups in numerical simulations while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: Tensor train methods are effective for reducing computational costs in turbulent flow simulations, with potential applications in engineering.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas
authors: Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, And Alessio Celi
abstract:

Topological gauge theories constitute a framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in terms of weakly interacting composite degrees of freedom. Their topological properties become evident when these theories are realized on a space of nontrivial topology. Here, we propose a schem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023242] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a topological gauge theory on a ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose gas, focusing on synthetic dimensions and topological phases.
motivation: To explore topological gauge theories in a cold-atom platform with nontrivial spatial topology, enabling the study of strongly correlated quantum matter.
method: The authors design a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to create synthetic dimensions, effectively realizing a lattice gauge theory.
result: They demonstrate that the system can encode a topological gauge theory, with observable signatures such as chiral edge currents.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable experimental platform for studying topological gauge theories and their properties in ultracold atomic gases.

title: Straintronics And Twistronics In Bilayer Graphene
authors: Federico Escudero, Dong Wang, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Shengjun Yuan, Francisco Guinea, And Zhen Zhan

While magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene has been widely studied, strain provides an additional and realistic control knob for band engineerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023225] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay of strain and twist in bilayer graphene to engineer moiré patterns and narrow bands for correlated and topological phases.
motivation: To explore strain as an additional control knob beyond twist angle for band engineering in bilayer graphene, enabling new correlated and topological phases.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of strained and twisted bilayer graphene, analyzing band structures and moiré patterns.
result: Strain can significantly modify the moiré pattern and narrow band properties, offering a tunable platform for correlated and topological phases.
conclusion: Straintronics and twistronics together provide a versatile approach to engineer quantum phases in bilayer graphene.

title: Taxonomy Of Prediction
authors: Alexandra Jurgens And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandra Jurgens and James P. Crutchfield

A prediction makes a claim about a system's future given knowledge of its past. A retrodiction makes a claim about its past given knowledge of its future. The bidirectional machine is an ambidextrous hidden Markov chain that does both optimally by making explicit in its state structure all statistic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023218] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a taxonomy of prediction and retrodiction using bidirectional hidden Markov chains, focusing on optimal inference from past and future data.
motivation: To systematically classify and unify different types of prediction and retrodiction in stochastic processes, and to characterize their computational and statistical properties.
method: The authors develop the bidirectional machine, a hidden Markov model that optimally performs both prediction and retrodiction by incorporating all relevant statistical information from past and future observations.
result: They derive a taxonomy of prediction types based on the structure of the bidirectional machine and demonstrate its optimality in terms of predictive accuracy and model complexity.
conclusion: The bidirectional machine provides a unified framework for understanding prediction and retrodiction, with implications for statistical inference and computational mechanics.

title: Symmetry And Self-bound Droplets In Dipolar Molecular Gases
authors: D. Baillie

We reveal a symmetry structure of the dipolar interaction that generates degeneracies among the interaction parameters, en…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023219] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies symmetry and self-bound droplets in dipolar molecular gases, focusing on the role of engineered anisotropy in dipolar interactions.
motivation: Recent experiments with microwave-dressed molecular gases allow control of dipolar interactions, motivating a theoretical study of symmetry structures and droplet formation.
method: The authors analyze the symmetry of the dipolar interaction under elliptical polarization, revealing degeneracies among interaction parameters, and use mean-field theory to model self-bound droplets.
result: They find that the symmetry leads to new classes of self-bound droplets with tunable properties, and identify parameter regimes where droplets are stable.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding and controlling dipolar droplet formation in molecular gases, with implications for quantum simulation.

title: Quantum Optical Electron Pulse Shaper
authors: Neli Laštovičková Streshkova And Martin Kozák

method: An optical pulse shaper is used to modulate the envelope and phase of an electron beam via the ponderomotive potential in a laser field.
result: Experimental demonstration of shaping electron pulses with controlled temporal and spectral properties.
conclusion: This technique opens new possibilities for ultrafast electron microscopy and quantum control of electron matter waves.

For example, in a nonreciprocal mixture of two species, changing the average density of either species alters the…

tldr: This paper studies compositional disorder and pattern formation in a multicomponent nonreciprocal mixture, focusing on stability and phase behavior.
motivation: Understanding how nonreciprocal interactions affect phase separation and pattern formation in active mixtures is of fundamental interest in soft matter and active matter physics.
method: The authors use linear stability analysis and numerical simulations to investigate the stability of homogeneous states and the emergence of patterns in a multicomponent nonreciprocal mixture.
result: They find that compositional disorder can lead to novel pattern formation and that the stability boundaries depend on the average densities and nonreciprocity strength.
conclusion: The work extends concepts from passive phase separation to active nonreciprocal systems, revealing rich dynamical behavior.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:

motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; the authors aim to leverage physical principles to improve link prediction.
method: The paper develops a framework that incorporates physical constraints and dynamics to infer causal links from observational data.
result: The framework demonstrates improved accuracy in predicting physical links across various networked systems.
conclusion: Physics-informed approaches can enhance causal inference in networks, with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers

motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in fractional quantum Hall systems beyond the conventional paradigm.
method: Theoretical analysis using field theory and numerical methods for quantum Hall bilayers near a topological phase transition.
result: Anyonic excitons form a superfluid phase with unique properties at the critical point.
conclusion: Topological criticality provides a robust mechanism for engineering anyonic superfluids in quantum Hall bilayers.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart

result: The system exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the magnetic properties of kagome ice systems and the role of universality in frustrated magnets.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe

motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré systems.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: The experiment reveals a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and shows electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism, relevant for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations yet high susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly simulations to analyze the critical properties of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show suppressed critical opalescence but enhanced susceptibility, leading to a unique critical point.
conclusion: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit a distinct type of criticality that challenges standard theories of liquid-gas phase transitions.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize scattering and radiative loss.
result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniform designs for photonic applications and suggest new design rules.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using electron optics for coherent spin control.
motivation: To achieve gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and coherent spin control in graphene for spintronic applications.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene is used to reveal ballistic spin transport and spin-dependent electron optics.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.
conclusion: The work provides a mechanism for coherent spin control in graphene, advancing spintronics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.

motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state may explain their unique properties.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical methods to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: They identify a dipolar nematic state and describe its properties.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Increasing microscopic activity in a sparse active solid can counterintuitively reduce its macroscopic active response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how the density of active units affects the collective mechanical response in active solids.
method: Combined experiments with robotic metamaterials and theoretical modeling.
result: When active units are too sparse, increasing activity does not percolate, causing the macroscopic active response to vanish.
conclusion: The phenomenon 'more is less' arises from percolation thresholds in active solids.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation

abstract:

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: To provide a systematic and experimentally feasible approach for generating complex multimode multi-photon quantum states.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to express target states as a combination of simpler states, then realize them via photon catalysis with linear optics and postselection.
result: They show that any photonic state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a general and efficient recipe for photonic state preparation, advancing quantum optics experiments.

title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks Are Effectively Classically Simulable
authors: Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Bermejo, Paolo Braccia, Manuel S. Rudolph, Zoë Holmes, Lukasz Cincio, and M. Cerezo

The action of a quantum convolutional neural network, which is a promising architecture for quantum machine learning, can be efficiently simulated by a classical computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020304] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: Quantum convolutional neural networks can be efficiently simulated classically, limiting their quantum advantage.
motivation: Quantum machine learning promises speedups, but it is crucial to identify which architectures actually provide quantum advantage.
method: The authors analyze the structure of quantum convolutional neural networks and show that their action can be simulated efficiently on a classical computer.
result: Quantum convolutional neural networks are effectively classically simulable, meaning they do not offer a quantum advantage.
conclusion: This work highlights the need for careful benchmarking of quantum machine learning models to avoid overclaiming quantum advantage.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged established theories.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: It covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and magneto-optical interactions.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving with expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and application directions.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new electronic states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field theory.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic techniques such as path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theory provides a unified framework for analyzing these systems, including examples from chemical reactions and population dynamics.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are powerful tools for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond physics.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a paradigmatic model for complex systems, and understanding their dynamics is crucial for many fields.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical developments, and large-scale numerical simulations.
result: It tracks progress in spin-glass dynamics from inception to present, highlighting synergies between approaches.
conclusion: Spin-glass research remains active with future opportunities, but the paper does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic and topological properties.
result: Highlights key materials and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future work.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for modeling neural networks, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion; understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current theoretical methods and identifies open challenges in accurately modeling internal conversion.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to better predict and control internal conversion in molecular systems for photonic and energy harvesting applications.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum depinning and skyrmion qubits.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with potential for quantum information but remains largely exploratory.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including possible mediators and connections to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions.
method: Review of theoretical models for exotic boson-mediated interactions and experimental techniques for detecting spin-dependent forces.
result: Summarizes current constraints on various spin-dependent interaction parameters and outlines future experimental directions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential to reveal new physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects like decoherence and entanglement.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts to detect gravity-induced decoherence, collapse, and entanglement between massive particles.
result: Summarizes current state-of-the-art experiments and theoretical models for testing quantum gravity with massive quantum systems.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further experimental and theoretical work is needed.

title: Ultracold Neutron Energy Spectrum And Storage Properties From Magnetically Induced Spin Depolarization
authors: N. J. Ayres et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): N. J. Ayres et al. (nEDM Collaboration at PSI)

We present a novel method for extracting the energy spectrum of ultracold neutrons from magnetically induced spin depolarization measurements using the n2EDM apparatus. This method is also used to exploit sensitivity to the storage properties of the materials used to trap ultracold neutrons, specifi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221902] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A method to extract ultracold neutron energy spectra from spin depolarization measurements in the n2EDM apparatus.
motivation: Understanding ultracold neutron energy spectra and storage properties is important for neutron electric dipole moment experiments.
method: Magnetically induced spin depolarization measurements are used to infer the energy spectrum and storage properties of ultracold neutrons.
result: The method provides a novel way to characterize ultracold neutron sources and storage materials.
conclusion: This technique can improve the design and analysis of future neutron EDM experiments.

Acoustic magnetochiral anisotropy is observed in a diamagnetic crystal of

motivation: To demonstrate a new magneto-acoustic effect analogous to magnetochiral anisotropy in optics.
method: Experimental measurement of acoustic wave propagation in α quartz under magnetic field.
result: Acoustic magnetochiral anisotropy is observed, showing direction-dependent acoustic properties.
conclusion: The effect is a classical wave phenomenon with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unveiling Spin And Poynting Dual Textures Of An Optical Skyrmionic Tube In Free Space
authors: Sicong Wang, Zhikai Zhou, Yongjie Zhu, Jialin Sun, Jiahui Mao, Minghui Wang, Shichao Song, Zi-Lan Deng, Yaoyu Cao, Fei Qin, Yunkun Wu, Xifeng Ren, And Xiangping Li
abstract:
Author(s): Sicong Wang, Zhikai Zhou, Yongjie Zhu, Jialin Sun, Jiahui Mao, Minghui Wang, Shichao Song, Zi-lan Deng, Yaoyu Cao, Fei Qin, Yunkun Wu, Xifeng Ren, and Xiangping Li

Optical skyrmions are topological textures of electromagnetic fields with promising applications in information processing, transport, and storage. Exquisitely tailoring the optical fields of diverse physical quantities has expanded the family of skyrmions, yet such skyrmions only exhibit a single-q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223803] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the experimental observation of an optical skyrmionic tube in free space, revealing spin and Poynting dual textures.
motivation: Optical skyrmions are topological textures with potential for information processing, but previous demonstrations were limited to single-quantity skyrmions. The authors aim to realize a skyrmionic tube with dual textures.
method: The authors design and fabricate a photonic chip to generate a structured light field that forms a skyrmionic tube, and measure its spin and Poynting vector distributions.
result: They observe a skyrmionic tube with both spin and Poynting dual textures, confirming the topological structure.
conclusion: This work expands the family of optical skyrmions and may enable new applications in information transport and storage.

title: Electron Recoil Via Sample Momentum Transfer In Optical-Mode Excitation
authors: Akira Yasuhara, Yamato Kirii, And Takumi Sannomiya
abstract:
Author(s): Akira Yasuhara, Yamato Kirii, and Takumi Sannomiya

Momentum-resolved EELS provides the first direct evidence that electrons impart measurable momentum to planar samples during mode excitation.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226901] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental evidence of electron recoil via momentum transfer to planar samples during optical-mode excitation using momentum-resolved EELS.
motivation: To directly demonstrate that electrons impart measurable momentum to samples during mode excitation, which is a fundamental aspect of electron-matter interaction.
method: Momentum-resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) is used to measure the momentum transfer from electrons to planar samples upon optical-mode excitation.
result: First direct evidence that electrons transfer measurable momentum to planar samples during mode excitation.
conclusion: The findings confirm momentum transfer in electron-sample interactions, which may have implications for understanding energy and momentum exchange in nanoscale systems.

title: Macroscopic Illusion And Microscopic Reality Of Glass Formation Paths: Cooling Vs Compression
authors: Kajetan Koperwas, Żaneta Wojnarowska, And Marian Paluch
abstract:
Author(s): Kajetan Koperwas, Żaneta Wojnarowska, and Marian Paluch

We provide evidence that dynamical slowdown in glass-forming liquids may follow different microscopic routes under cooling and compression, pointing to a previously unrecognized discrepancy between two dynamical landmarks: the Arrhenius–to–non-Arrhenius crossover associated with cooling and the infl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 228001] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the microscopic dynamics of glass formation under cooling versus compression, revealing a discrepancy in the Arrhenius-to-non-Arrhenius crossover.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic routes of dynamical slowdown in glass-forming liquids is important for materials science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors compare experimental and simulation data for glass-forming liquids under cooling and compression, analyzing dynamical landmarks.
result: They find that the crossover temperature under cooling differs from the crossover pressure under compression, indicating different microscopic mechanisms.
conclusion: The work highlights a previously unrecognized discrepancy in glass formation paths, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Altermagnetic And Dipolar Splitting Of Magnons In ${\mathrm{FeF}}_{2}$
authors: J. Sears, V. O. Garlea, D. Lederman, J. M. Tranquada, And I. A. Zaliznyak
abstract:
Author(s): J. Sears, V. O. Garlea, D. Lederman, J. M. Tranquada, and I. A. Zaliznyak

Neutron scattering measurements show that altermagnetic splitting of chiral magnons in the classical antiferromagnet FeF
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226701] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering study of magnon splitting in FeF2, comparing altermagnetic and dipolar effects.
motivation: To understand the relative contributions of altermagnetic and dipolar interactions to magnon splitting in a classical antiferromagnet.
method: Neutron scattering measurements on FeF2 single crystals, analyzing magnon dispersion and splitting.
result: Altermagnetic splitting is small compared to dipolar splitting in FeF2.
conclusion: Dipolar interactions dominate the magnon splitting in this material, overshadowing altermagnetic effects.

title: Accurate Boundary Bootstrap For The Three-Dimensional $\mathrm{O}(N)$ Normal Universality Class
authors: Runzhe Hu And Wenliang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Runzhe Hu and Wenliang Li

The three-dimensional classical [MATH] model with a boundary has received renewed interest due to the discovery of the extraordinary-log boundary universality class for [MATH]. The critical value [MATH] and the exponent of the boundary correlation function are related to certai…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221601] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the boundary critical behavior of the 3D O(N) model using conformal bootstrap methods.
motivation: To understand the extraordinary-log boundary universality class and compute critical exponents for the O(N) model with a boundary.
method: The authors use the numerical conformal bootstrap to solve crossing equations for boundary correlators, focusing on the normal universality class.
result: They obtain precise estimates for the critical value N_c and the exponent of the boundary correlation function.
conclusion: The work provides accurate bootstrap results for the 3D O(N) boundary model, contributing to the understanding of boundary critical phenomena.

title: Coherent Radiation Of Multielectron Wave Packets In Intense Laser Fields
authors: Dejia Dai, Xiaofei Shen, And Bin Qiao
abstract:
Author(s): Dejia Dai, Xiaofei Shen, and Bin Qiao

Coherent radiation from laser-driven electron beams can serve as a light source. In this work, we investigate the coherent radiation emitted by a multielectron system interacting with a plane-wave electromagnetic pulse in the framework of strong-field QED. Using the density matrix formalism, we gene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063105] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Investigates coherent radiation from multielectron wave packets in intense laser fields using strong-field QED and density matrix formalism.
motivation: To understand and characterize coherent radiation from laser-driven electron beams as a potential light source.
method: Uses density matrix formalism within strong-field QED to model a multielectron system interacting with a plane-wave electromagnetic pulse.
result: Derives general expressions for coherent radiation and analyzes the effects of electron correlations and wave packet structure.
conclusion: Coherent radiation properties depend on the multielectron wave packet dynamics, offering insights for advanced light source design.

title: Second-order Correlations In Directed Emissions In Sodium Atoms
authors: Ara Tonoyan, Sushree Subhadarshinee Sahoo, Anahit Gogyan, Oleg Tretiak, Razmik Aramyan, Alexander Akulshin, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Ara Tonoyan, Sushree Subhadarshinee Sahoo, Anahit Gogyan, Oleg Tretiak, Razmik Aramyan, Alexander Akulshin, and Dmitry Budker

We report second-order intensity correlations [MATH] of directional midinfrared emissions from sodium vapor under bichromatic continuous-wave excitation. Directional emission at [MATH] in the forward direction and at $2.21{0ex}}µ\m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063710] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports second-order intensity correlations of directional mid-infrared emissions from sodium vapor under bichromatic excitation.
motivation: To study the quantum statistical properties of directional emissions from atomic vapors, which may have applications in quantum optics and metrology.
method: Experimental measurement of second-order correlation functions g(2)(τ) of mid-infrared light emitted from sodium vapor under continuous-wave bichromatic excitation.
result: Observation of second-order correlations in the directional emissions, indicating non-classical or classical statistical behavior depending on experimental conditions.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the coherence and correlation properties of atomic vapor emissions, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Bidirectional Feedback And Correlation Analysis Of Soliton-state Transitions Mediated By A Quasi-continuous-wave Background
authors: Xin Yan, Wen-Zhi Lan, Zhen-Tao Ju, Hao-Yu Feng, Hui-Jun Li, Yue-Yue Wang, And Chao-Qing Dai
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Yan, Wen-Zhi Lan, Zhen-Tao Ju, Hao-Yu Feng, Hui-Jun Li, Yue-Yue Wang, and Chao-Qing Dai

The quasi-continuous-wave background (qCWB) is a common phenomenon in the nonlinear dynamics of ultrafast fiber lasers, yet its role in soliton-state transitions remains insufficiently understood. Here, we confirm the presence of qCWB by combining soliton filtering with short-time Fourier transform …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063511] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies soliton-state transitions in ultrafast fiber lasers mediated by a quasi-continuous-wave background, using bidirectional feedback and correlation analysis.
motivation: The role of quasi-continuous-wave background in soliton-state transitions is not well understood, and the authors aim to clarify its influence.
method: The authors combine soliton filtering with short-time Fourier transform to confirm the presence of qCWB and analyze its correlation with soliton dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that qCWB mediates transitions between different soliton states and provide a feedback mechanism explaining the observed correlations.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of nonlinear dynamics in fiber lasers, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Controlling Resonant Spin Photocurrent Using Magnetic Field: Application To The Magnetoelectric Oxide ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$
authors: Zhuo-Cheng Gu And Hiroaki Ishizuka
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuo-Cheng Gu and Hiroaki Ishizuka

Controlling magnons in magnetic insulators is key to their application in spintronics. In this work, we study the magnon spin photocurrent in effective spin models for [MATH], a material known for its magnetoelectric (ME) effect. Using the nonlinear response theory, we s…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon spin photocurrent in Cr2O3 using nonlinear response theory, focusing on spintronics applications.
motivation: Controlling magnons in magnetic insulators is key for spintronics; the magnetoelectric oxide Cr2O3 offers a platform for such control via magnetic fields.
method: The authors use nonlinear response theory to compute the magnon spin photocurrent in effective spin models for Cr2O3.
result: They find that the spin photocurrent can be controlled by an external magnetic field, demonstrating a mechanism for magnon-based current generation.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for spin photocurrent in magnetoelectric materials, potentially useful for spintronic devices.

title: Magnetic Field Induced Modification Of A First-order Ferromagnetic Transition In ${\mathrm{Eu}}_{2}\mathrm{In}$
authors: Ajay Kumar, Anis Biswas, Trevor A. Tyson, Daniel Haskel, Christopher J. Pollock, And Yaroslav Mudryk

We present a comprehensive study of the temperature- and magnetic-field-dependent magnetization, specific heat, and local crystal structure across the first-order ferromagnetic–paramagnetic transition in [MATH]. Anomalies in the magnetocaloric response are observed near $H≈25…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214421] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the magnetic field-induced modification of a first-order ferromagnetic transition in Eu2In, focusing on magnetocaloric effects and local crystal structure.
motivation: To understand the interplay between magnetic field, temperature, and structural changes in a ferromagnetic material with potential magnetocaloric applications.
method: Temperature- and field-dependent magnetization, specific heat, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy measurements were performed to probe the transition and local structure.
result: Anomalies in the magnetocaloric response near H≈25 kOe indicate a field-induced modification of the first-order transition, correlated with changes in local crystal structure.
conclusion: The study reveals a complex coupling between magnetic and structural degrees of freedom in Eu2In, relevant for understanding magnetocaloric materials.

title: Fragile Long-range Antiferromagnetic Order In The Triangular-lattice Quantum Magnet ${\mathrm{ErZn}}_{3}{\mathrm{P}}_{3}$
authors: Yimin Wang, Peiyue Ma, Weijie Lin, Ye Xia, Yujie Wang, Ruixiang Jiang, Xinlei Liu, Chaoxin Huang, Tao Xie, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yimin Wang, Peiyue Ma, Weijie Lin, Ye Xia, Yujie Wang, Ruixiang Jiang, Xinlei Liu, Chaoxin Huang, Tao Xie, and Meng Wang

Rare-earth triangular lattices provide an ideal platform for exploring novel quantum magnetic states. Here, we report the crystal growth and magnetic properties of a rare-earth triangular-lattice compound, [MATH]. Alternating-current magnetic susceptibility and specifi…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214422] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the crystal growth and magnetic properties of a rare-earth triangular-lattice compound ErZn3P3, revealing fragile long-range antiferromagnetic order.
motivation: Rare-earth triangular lattices are platforms for exploring novel quantum magnetic states, but the magnetic properties of ErZn3P3 were previously unknown.
method: Single crystals were grown, and magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and neutron diffraction measurements were performed to characterize the magnetic order.
result: The compound exhibits long-range antiferromagnetic order below 2.5 K, but the order is fragile and easily suppressed by magnetic fields.
conclusion: ErZn3P3 is a candidate for studying frustrated magnetism on a triangular lattice, but its properties are not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Ramp Josephson Junctions Of Al/Ti/$\mathrm{S}{\mathrm{r}}_{2}\mathrm{Ru}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$: Observation Of Single-domain Quantum Oscillations And The Detection Of Chiral Surface Current
authors: Zixuan Li, Yiqun Alex Ying, Brian M. Zakrzewski, Yan Xin, Yu Wang, Zhiqiang Mao, And Ying Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zixuan Li, Yiqun Alex Ying, Brian M. Zakrzewski, Yan Xin, Yu Wang, Zhiqiang Mao, and Ying Liu

The determination of how the phase of the superconducting order parameter in a superconductor varies with the spatial direction, which can be done only through Josephson-effect-based phase-sensitive measurements, is crucial for the establishment of the precise pairing symmetry of the superconductor.…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214510] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports phase-sensitive measurements on ramp Josephson junctions of Al/Ti/Sr2RuO4 to detect chiral surface currents and determine the pairing symmetry of Sr2RuO4.
motivation: The pairing symmetry of Sr2RuO4 remains controversial; phase-sensitive Josephson measurements are crucial to determine the order parameter symmetry and detect chiral surface currents.
method: Ramp Josephson junctions of Al/Ti/Sr2RuO4 were fabricated and their quantum oscillations were measured to probe the phase variation of the superconducting order parameter.
result: Single-domain quantum oscillations were observed, providing evidence for chiral surface currents and constraining the pairing symmetry.
conclusion: The results support a chiral order parameter in Sr2RuO4, advancing the understanding of its unconventional superconductivity.

title: V $3d$ And Se $4p$ Spectral Reconstruction By Charge Density Wave Formation In ${\mathrm{VSe}}_{2}$ Probed By Angle-resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy
authors: K. Fujinuma, T. Hara, M. Emi, N. Katayama, H. Sawa, X. Zhao, K. Takubo, G. Tomassucci, F. Minati, A. Barinov, K. Ozawa, N. L. Saini, And T. Mizokawa
abstract:
Author(s): K. Fujinuma, T. Hara, M. Emi, N. Katayama, H. Sawa, X. Zhao, K. Takubo, G. Tomassucci, F. Minati, A. Barinov, K. Ozawa, N. L. Saini, and T. Mizokawa

The electronic structure of [MATH] with [MATH] charge density wave (CDW) transition has been studied by means of angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and scanning photoemission microscopy (SPEM). The partial depletion of the Fermi surfaces is observed in the CDW phase …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235112] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: ARPES study of VSe2 reveals spectral reconstruction due to charge density wave formation.
motivation: To understand the electronic structure changes associated with the charge density wave transition in VSe2.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and scanning photoemission microscopy (SPEM) were used to probe the electronic structure.
result: Partial depletion of Fermi surfaces is observed in the CDW phase, indicating spectral reconstruction of V 3d and Se 4p states.
conclusion: The CDW formation significantly modifies the electronic structure, consistent with a Peierls-like mechanism.

title: Percolative Pathway To Stripe Order In ${\mathrm{KTaO}}_{3}$-based Superconductivity
authors: Zhihao Chen, Chun Sum Brian Pang, Meng Yang, Yuxin Wang, Huaiyuan Wang, He Zheng, Kun Jiang, Bruce A. Davidson, Ilya Elfimov, George A. Sawatzky, Andrea Damascelli, Ke Zou, And Zhi Gang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Zhihao Chen, Chun Sum Brian Pang, Meng Yang, Yuxin Wang, Huaiyuan Wang, He Zheng, Kun Jiang, Bruce A. Davidson, Ilya Elfimov, George A. Sawatzky, Andrea Damascelli, Ke Zou, and Zhi Gang Cheng

The sensitivity of low-dimensional superconductors to fluctuations gives rise to emergent behaviors beyond the conventional Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer framework. Anisotropy is one such manifestation often linked to spatially modulated electronic responses and unconventional pairing mechanisms. Pronou…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245115] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stripe order and superconductivity in KTaO3-based heterostructures, focusing on percolative pathways and anisotropic transport.
motivation: To understand emergent superconducting behavior in low-dimensional systems and the role of anisotropy and stripe order.
method: Experimental transport measurements and scanning probe microscopy on KTaO3-based interfaces, combined with theoretical modeling.
result: Observation of percolative stripe order that correlates with superconducting properties.
conclusion: Stripe order and percolation play a key role in the unconventional superconductivity of KTaO3-based systems.

title: Anomalies In The Thermal Conductivity Of The Honeycomb Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPS}}_{3}$
authors: Jian Yan, Hiromu Okamoto, Hiroki Yoshida, Hikaru Takeda, Xuan Luo, Yuping Sun, Jun-Ichi Yamaura, And Minoru Yamashita
abstract:
Author(s): Jian Yan, Hiromu Okamoto, Hiroki Yoshida, Hikaru Takeda, Xuan Luo, Yuping Sun, Jun-ichi Yamaura, and Minoru Yamashita

Intrinsic two-dimensional magnets serve as a good platform to explore collective, charge-neutral, and low-energy excitations. Distinguishing their crucial role in the experimental aspect remains a challenge for decades. Here, we study the thermal transport in honeycomb antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPS…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal transport anomalies in the honeycomb antiferromagnet MnPS3, focusing on low-energy excitations.
motivation: To understand the role of collective charge-neutral excitations in thermal transport of two-dimensional magnets.
method: Thermal conductivity measurements on MnPS3 single crystals.
result: Observed anomalies in thermal conductivity attributed to magnon-phonon interactions or spin fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into low-energy excitations in 2D antiferromagnets but have no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Phase Transitions And Electrical Conductivity Of Selenium Disulfide At High Pressure
authors: Huixin Hu, Israel Osmond, Calum Strain, Hannah A. Shuttleworth, Callum R. Stevens, Andrew Huxley, Mikhail A. Kuzovnikov, Federico A. Gorelli, Eugene Gregoryanz, Miriam Peña-Alvarez, Philip Dalladay-Simpson, And Ross T. Howie
abstract:

Sulfur and selenium demonstrate one of the most complex behavior under high pressure among all elements of the periodic table. Despite being known to form interchalcogens, the properties of these compounds have not been widely explored in the dense state. Through a series of diamond anvil experiment…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214101] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase transitions and electrical conductivity of selenium disulfide under high pressure using diamond anvil cell experiments.
motivation: To explore the high-pressure behavior of interchalcogen compounds, which are less studied than pure sulfur or selenium.
method: Diamond anvil cell experiments combined with electrical conductivity measurements and structural characterization.
result: Observed pressure-induced phase transitions and changes in electrical conductivity in selenium disulfide.
conclusion: The high-pressure properties of selenium disulfide reveal complex behavior, but the work is primarily a materials science study without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Simplified Approach For Atomistic Modeling Of Magnetic Nanostructures By Scaling The Lattice Constant
authors: A. W. Teixeira, D. Altbir, S. Castillo-Sepúlveda, R. M. Corona, D. Laroze, And V. L. Carvalho-Santos
abstract:
Author(s): A. W. Teixeira, D. Altbir, S. Castillo-Sepúlveda, R. M. Corona, D. Laroze, and V. L. Carvalho-Santos

Computational simulations are an important tool for understanding the magnetic properties of nanostructures that complement both experimental and analytical techniques. Among the different numerical techniques, micromagnetism offers tools for large systems; however, it presents difficulties when dea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224415] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a simplified computational method for atomistic modeling of magnetic nanostructures by scaling the lattice constant.
motivation: Atomistic simulations of magnetic nanostructures are computationally expensive; the authors aim to reduce cost while preserving accuracy.
method: They propose scaling the lattice constant to reduce the number of atoms, and validate the approach by comparing with full atomistic and micromagnetic simulations.
result: The scaled lattice constant method reproduces key magnetic properties (e.g., hysteresis, domain structure) with significantly lower computational cost.
conclusion: The method offers a practical trade-off between accuracy and efficiency for modeling large magnetic nanostructures.

title: Quantum Tunneling Driven Giant Electric Field Gradients In Plasmonic Cavities
authors: Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, And Wending Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, and Wending Zhang

Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing in plasmonic cavities while significantly enhancing the electric field gradient. This study employs a plasmonic cavity to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile, directly observing this phenomenon via the quadrupole-to-dipol…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235108] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum tunneling in plasmonic cavities and its effect on electric field gradients, observed via multipolar Raman scattering.
motivation: To understand how quantum tunneling affects extreme nanofocusing and field gradients in plasmonic cavities.
method: The authors use a plasmonic cavity to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile and analyze the quadrupole-to-dipole transition.
result: Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing but significantly enhances the electric field gradient.
conclusion: The enhanced field gradient due to quantum tunneling can be exploited for sensing or spectroscopy applications.

title: Signatures Of Kondo-lattice Behavior In The Two-dimensional Ferromagnet ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GeTe}}_{2}$
authors: Carmen Rubio-Verdú And Katharina J. Franke
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235410] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo-lattice behavior in a 2D ferromagnet using STM/STS, focusing on magnetic interactions rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the microscopic magnetic interactions in Fe3GeTe2, a van der Waals magnet with debated magnetic properties.
method: Scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy at 1.1 K to map low-energy electronic states on the surface.
result: Observed signatures of Kondo-lattice behavior, indicating coupling between localized magnetic moments and conduction electrons.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the magnetic interactions in Fe3GeTe2, but are not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Impact Of Multiband Effects On non-Fermi-liquid Transport Phenomena In Bilayer Nickelates
authors: Seiichiro Onari, Daisuke Inoue, Rina Tazai, Youichi Yamakawa, And Hiroshi Kontani
abstract:

Recently discovered high-[MATH] superconductivity in thin-film bilayer nickelates [MATH] under ambient pressure has attracted great interest. Non-Fermi-liquid transport behaviors, such as [MATH]-linear resistivity and a positive Hall coefficient that inc…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245110] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Fermi-liquid transport in bilayer nickelates, focusing on multiband effects and superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the anomalous transport properties observed in recently discovered high-temperature superconducting bilayer nickelates.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and analysis of multiband electronic structure to explain non-Fermi-liquid behaviors such as T-linear resistivity and positive Hall coefficient.
result: They find that multiband effects are crucial for reproducing the observed transport anomalies.
conclusion: Multiband correlations play a key role in the non-Fermi-liquid transport and superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.

title: Valley-dependent Electron-phonon Scattering In Thermoelectric Semimetal ${\mathrm{Ta}}_{2}{\mathrm{PdSe}}_{6}$
authors: Masayuki Ochi, Hitoshi Mori, And Akitoshi Nakano
abstract:
Author(s): Masayuki Ochi, Hitoshi Mori, and Akitoshi Nakano

Quasi-one-dimensional transition-metal chalcogenide [MATH] is a promising thermoelectric semimetal due to the strong electron-hole asymmetry in the carrier lifetime. However, the microscopic origin of such a strong asymmetry remains unclear. In this study, we theoreti…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245112] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies valley-dependent electron-phonon scattering in a thermoelectric semimetal, focusing on carrier lifetime asymmetry.
motivation: To understand the microscopic origin of strong electron-hole asymmetry in carrier lifetime in Ta2PdSe6, which is important for thermoelectric performance.
method: First-principles calculations and Boltzmann transport theory to compute electron-phonon scattering rates and carrier lifetimes.
result: Valley-dependent scattering leads to significantly different lifetimes for electrons and holes, explaining the observed asymmetry.
conclusion: The valley-dependent electron-phonon scattering is the key mechanism behind the thermoelectric properties of Ta2PdSe6.

title: Biased Continuous-time Random Walks With Asymmetric Waiting-time Distributions As A Model Of Anomalous Diffusion In The Presence Of Drift
authors: Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, And Ralf Metzler
abstract:
Author(s): Guohua Li, Andrey G. Cherstvy, Wenya Guo, Hong Zhang, Ting Liu, Wendong Pu, and Ralf Metzler

Mathematical models of diffusion based on stochastic processes of the type of continuous-time random walks (CTRWs) are widely used for the description of various transport characteristics in complex media. An external or internal bias in a given CTRW model is often attributed to an asymmetric distri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper models anomalous diffusion with drift using biased continuous-time random walks with asymmetric waiting-time distributions.
motivation: To understand transport in complex media where external bias leads to asymmetric waiting times and anomalous diffusion.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of CTRW with asymmetric waiting-time distributions and drift, deriving mean squared displacement and other transport characteristics.
result: The model captures subdiffusive, superdiffusive, and normal diffusion regimes depending on the waiting-time distribution parameters and bias strength.
conclusion: Biased CTRWs with asymmetric waiting times provide a versatile framework for describing anomalous diffusion in the presence of drift.

title: Reinforcement Learning For Chemotherapy Scheduling In A Stochastic Tumor Evolution Model
authors: M. Giles And P. K. Newton

Author(s): M. Giles and P. K. Newton

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064404] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Uses reinforcement learning to optimize chemotherapy dosing schedules in a stochastic tumor evolution model.
motivation: To improve cancer treatment by finding optimal drug schedules that minimize tumor burden while accounting for drug resistance.
method: Applies Q-learning, a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm, to a stochastic finite-cell model of tumor evolution with three competing subpopulations.
result: The RL agent learns dosing schedules that outperform standard protocols in simulations.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning is a promising tool for personalized chemotherapy scheduling, but further validation is needed.

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Zhao and Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature. Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, particularly when measuring observables affected by pa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exchange Monte Carlo method for continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo simulations to reduce autocorrelation times.
motivation: Traditional path integral Monte Carlo methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, especially for observables affected by permutation sampling.
method: The authors propose an exchange Monte Carlo algorithm that swaps configurations between multiple replicas at different temperatures to improve sampling efficiency.
result: The method reduces autocorrelation times and improves the accuracy of measurements in continuous-space PIMC simulations.
conclusion: Exchange Monte Carlo is an effective technique for enhancing sampling in continuous-space PIMC, enabling more efficient simulations of bosonic systems.

title: Further Testing The Validity Of Generalized Heterogeneous-elasticity Theory For Low-frequency Excitations In Structural Glasses
authors: Walter Schirmacher, Matteo Paoluzzi, Felix Cosmin Mocanu, Dmytro Khomenko, Gregorsz Szamel, Francesco Zamponi, And Giancarlo Ruocco

tldr: This paper tests the validity of generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory for low-frequency excitations in structural glasses, focusing on nonuniversal scaling of the vibrational density of states.
motivation: Understanding low-frequency vibrational excitations in glasses is important for their mechanical and thermal properties, but the universality of scaling laws is debated.
method: The authors summarize their previous theory and provide further computational evidence by analyzing the nonphononic vibrational density of states and its scaling behavior in model glasses.
result: They find nonuniversal scaling of the nonphononic density of states, challenging the universality of the ω^4 law.
conclusion: The generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory captures the observed nonuniversality, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Diffusion-driven Pattern Formation In An Opinion Dynamical Network Model
authors: Tim Mauch And Thilo Gross
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Mauch and Thilo Gross

The spatial organization of individuals and their interactions in communities are important factors known to preserve diversity in many complex systems. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 064302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A network model of opinion formation with spatial structure, inspired by ecological metapopulation models, studies pattern formation in opinion dynamics.
motivation: To understand how spatial organization and community interactions preserve diversity in opinion dynamics, using a metapopulation-inspired network approach.
method: Develops a network model where nodes represent communities and edges represent interactions, analyzing diffusion-driven pattern formation via dynamical systems and bifurcation analysis.
result: Identifies conditions under which spatial patterns of opinions emerge, showing that community structure can stabilize diverse opinions.
conclusion: Spatial organization and network topology play a key role in maintaining opinion diversity, with implications for social systems and collective behavior.

title: Free-energy Model Of Ferroelectric Transition In P(VDF-TrFE) Copolymer
authors: Vadim V. Atrazhev, Dmitry V. Dmitriev, And Vadim I. Sultanov

We develop a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in poly(vinylidene difluoride-co-trifluoroethylene) [P(VDF-TrFE)] copolymers. [Phys. Rev. E 113, 065405] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Develops a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers.
motivation: To understand the phase transition mechanism in ferroelectric polymers, which are important for applications like sensors and actuators.
method: Constructs a free-energy model based on the Landau-Devonshire theory, incorporating dipole interactions and thermal fluctuations.
result: The model reproduces the temperature dependence of polarization and dielectric constant, and predicts the transition temperature as a function of copolymer composition.
conclusion: The analytical model provides a quantitative description of the ferroelectric transition in P(VDF-TrFE) and can guide material design.

title: Externally Driven Condensates Show Translation-induced Polarization, Directed Coalescence, And Anomalous Diffusion In Viscoelastic Media
authors: Andriy Goychuk
abstract:
Author(s): Andriy Goychuk

Phase separation into compositionally and physically distinct domains is ubiquitous in (non)living matter ranging from alloys and emulsions to biomolecular condensates in cells. The organization of these domains can be controlled, for example, by nonequilibrium chemical reactions, external fields, o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065402] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase separation in externally driven condensates, focusing on polarization, coalescence, and anomalous diffusion in viscoelastic media.
motivation: Understanding how external driving forces control the organization and dynamics of phase-separated domains in soft matter and biological systems.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of condensate dynamics under external fields in viscoelastic environments.
result: External driving induces translation-induced polarization, directed coalescence, and anomalous diffusion of condensates.
conclusion: External fields can be used to control condensate organization, with implications for nonequilibrium soft matter and biological phase separation.

title: Resetting-induced Instability In Queues Fed By A Search Process In An Interval
authors: José Giral-Barajas And Paul C. Bressloff
abstract:
Author(s): José Giral-Barajas and Paul C. Bressloff

Proper management of resources whose arrival and consumption are subject to environmental randomness is an intrinsic process in both natural and artificial systems. This phenomenon can be modeled as a queuing process whose arrival distribution is determined by a search process with stochastic resett…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064101] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a queuing model where arrivals are governed by a search process with stochastic resetting, leading to instability.
motivation: To understand how resetting in search processes affects queue stability, relevant to resource management in random environments.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a queue fed by a search process with resetting, using generating functions and stability conditions.
result: Resetting can induce instability in the queue even when the underlying search process would otherwise be stable.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting can have counterintuitive effects on queue dynamics, with implications for natural and artificial systems.

title: Quantum Size Effect And Two-step Condensation Of Ideal Bose Atoms In An Optical Hard-wall Nanotube
authors: Ze Cheng
abstract:

tldr: The paper studies Bose-Einstein condensation in a quasi-1D optical nanotube with a hard-wall potential, focusing on quantum size effects and two-step condensation.
motivation: To understand how confinement and dimensionality affect Bose-Einstein condensation, particularly in a quasi-1D geometry with a hard-wall trap.
method: Theoretical analysis using the grand canonical ensemble and solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a quasi-1D harmonic potential combined with a 2D box trap.
result: Predicts a two-step condensation process and quantum size effects due to the discrete energy levels in the confined geometry.
conclusion: The quasi-1D system exhibits unique condensation behavior that could be observed in ultracold atom experiments.

title: Oscillatory Evolutionarily Stable State And Limit Cycle In Replicator Dynamics
authors: Suman Chakraborty, Vikash Kumar Dubey, Vaibhav Madhok, And Sagar Chakraborty
abstract:
Author(s): Suman Chakraborty, Vikash Kumar Dubey, Vaibhav Madhok, and Sagar Chakraborty

Such a state corresponds to a strategy adopted by the population such that a rare mutant strategy cannot invade …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062201] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillatory evolutionarily stable states and limit cycles in replicator dynamics from evolutionary game theory.
motivation: To extend the concept of evolutionarily stable states to non-equilibrium oscillatory behaviors in population dynamics.
method: Uses replicator dynamics and mathematical analysis to characterize oscillatory solutions and their stability.
result: Identifies conditions under which limit cycles can be evolutionarily stable, generalizing the static ESS concept.
conclusion: Oscillatory states can be stable under replicator dynamics, providing a richer framework for evolutionary game theory.

title: Kinetic Decoupling In Electron-beam-driven Dusty Plasma: Microscopic Randomization Coexisting With Collective Flow Stability
authors: Adrian Scurtu, Dorina Ticoş, Nicoleta Udrea, Maria L. Mitu, Beatrice Paraschiv, And Cătălin M. Ticoş

Energy injection and dissipation in nonequilibrium systems typically lock microscopic motion and collective flow into a coupled evolution. motivation: To understand energy injection and dissipation in non-equilibrium systems, specifically the breakdown of synchrony between microscopic motion and collective flow.
method: Experimental observations of electron-beam-driven dusty plasma, analyzing microscopic and collective dynamics.
result: Discovery of a kinetic decoupling regime where microscopic randomization and collective flow stability coexist.
conclusion: The findings reveal a distinct regime in dusty plasma that challenges typical coupled evolution assumptions.

title: Reducibility Of Higher-order To Pairwise Interactions: Social Impact Models On Hypergraphs
authors: Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, And Federico Vázquez
abstract:
Author(s): Jaume Llabrés, Raúl Toral, Maxi San Miguel, and Federico Vázquez

We show that a general class of node-update social impact models with higher-order interactions on hypergraphs can be exactly mapped to an equivalent model with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network. [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023250] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that higher-order social impact models on hypergraphs can be reduced to pairwise interactions on weighted projected networks.
motivation: To simplify the analysis of complex social systems with higher-order interactions by mapping them to well-understood pairwise models.
method: The authors prove an exact mapping from a class of node-update social impact models on hypergraphs to equivalent models with pairwise interactions on a weighted projected network, preserving microscopic transition probabilities.
result: The mapping is exact for the considered class of models, enabling the use of pairwise network tools to study higher-order social dynamics.
conclusion: Higher-order interactions in social impact models can be effectively reduced to pairwise interactions, simplifying theoretical and computational analysis.

title: Multiobjective Tweezers In Scattering Media
