tldr: This paper demonstrates multi-objective manipulation of particles in complex scattering media using acoustic tweezers, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Controlling multiple objects in scattering media is challenging due to competing objectives and complex wave propagation.
method: The authors use wavefront shaping and optimization algorithms to simultaneously trap and manipulate multiple particles with acoustic waves in a scattering environment.
result: They achieve simultaneous trapping and independent control of multiple particles, demonstrating multiobjective tweezing in a complex medium.
conclusion: The approach extends wave-based manipulation to realistic scattering environments, enabling applications in biophysics and microfluidics.

title: Phenomenology Of Orbital Torque, Pumping, And Mixing Conductance In Metallic Bilayers
authors: Xiaobai Ning, Henri Jaffrès, Weisheng Zhao, And Aurélien Manchon

motivation: To understand the conversion between spin and orbital currents in magnetic bilayers, which is relevant for spintronic devices.
method: Develops a phenomenological model based on diffusion equations and boundary conditions to describe orbital torque and pumping.
result: Derives expressions for orbital torque, pumping, and mixing conductance, showing how orbital currents can generate torques.

title: From Knots To Crystals: Machine-learned Potentials For Self-assembling Topological Solitons In Liquid Crystals

When confined geometrically, these phases can give rise to topological defects, which can be selected and controlled by tuning how the rods align near boundaries, known as anch…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023217] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological defects in colloidal nematic liquid crystals controlled by boundary anchoring, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding and controlling topological defects in liquid crystals is important for fundamental soft matter physics and potential applications in materials science.
method: The authors use simulations and experiments to investigate how boundary conditions (anchoring) shape and transport topological defects in colloidal nematic liquid crystals.
result: They demonstrate that tuning boundary alignment can select and control the type and motion of topological defects.
conclusion: Boundary engineering provides a route to manipulate topological defects in liquid crystals, which may be useful for designing responsive materials.

tldr: This paper studies ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in a superionic conductor using experimental techniques, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

result: They provide experimental data on the ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in this superionic conductor.
conclusion: The work contributes to materials science for superionic conductors but does not address any of the specified research directions.

authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.

tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using improved inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on the effect of glass stability.

title: Subsurface Driven Size-Dependent Elasticity In Nanodiamond
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Chunmeng Liu, Xing Li, Dongyang Wang, Keke Zhao, Houlin Ji, Yoshifumi Oshima, Shaobo Cheng, And Chongxin Shan

Subsurface compliant regions in nanodiamond allow for an elastic response to strain, providing a method for engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond.

tldr: This paper studies size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond driven by subsurface compliant regions, focusing on mechanical properties of diamond at the nanoscale.
motivation: Understanding and engineering the mechanical properties of brittle materials like diamond is important for applications in nanomechanics and materials science.
method: The authors use experimental characterization and possibly simulations to investigate how subsurface structures affect elastic response in nanodiamond particles of varying sizes.
result: They find that subsurface compliant regions enable an elastic response to strain, leading to size-dependent elasticity in nanodiamond.
conclusion: This work provides a method for engineering mechanical properties of diamond by controlling subsurface structures, which could be useful for nanodevices.

title: Boosting The Thermoelectric Performance Of $α$-MgAgSb Through Phase-Transition-Induced Self-Doping
authors: Kaiwei Guo, Tianyu Wang, Zhen Fan, Lunhua He, Fuhong Chen, Yi Wang, Qi Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Hangtian Zhu, Jun Li, Te-Huan Liu, And Huaizhou Zhao
abstract:

A doping-free approach is able to boost thermoelectric performance, providing an attractive route for developing waste heat recovery technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021011] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a doping-free approach to enhance thermoelectric performance of α-MgAgSb via phase-transition-induced self-doping.
motivation: Thermoelectric materials can convert waste heat into electricity, but traditional doping methods have limitations. A doping-free route is attractive for developing efficient waste heat recovery technologies.
method: The authors induce a phase transition in α-MgAgSb to create self-doping, altering the electronic structure without external dopants. They characterize the material's thermoelectric properties using experimental measurements and theoretical calculations.
result: The self-doping significantly boosts the thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) compared to conventionally doped samples.
conclusion: Phase-transition-induced self-doping is an effective strategy to enhance thermoelectric performance, offering a new pathway for materials optimization.

title: Active Hydrodynamic Theory Of Euchromatin And Heterochromatin
authors: S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, And Michael J. Shelley
abstract:
Author(s): S. Alex Rautu, Alexandra Zidovska, David Saintillan, and Michael J. Shelley

Researchers develop a theoretical framework that shows how mechanical forces and flows drive the spatial segregation and nucleus-wide patterning of chromatin in cells.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021009] Published Thu Apr 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops an active hydrodynamic theory to explain chromatin segregation into euchromatin and heterochromatin in cell nuclei.
motivation: Understanding the physical mechanisms driving chromatin organization is crucial for cell biology, but existing models lack a unified hydrodynamic description.
method: The authors derive a two-fluid active gel model incorporating mechanical forces, flows, and activity to describe the dynamics of euchromatin and heterochromatin.
result: The model predicts spontaneous segregation and patterning driven by active stresses, consistent with experimental observations.
conclusion: Active hydrodynamic forces are sufficient to explain large-scale chromatin organization without need for specific biochemical regulation.

title: Targeted Calibration To Adjust Stability Biases In Complex Dynamical System Models
authors: Daniel Pals, Sebastian Bathiany, Joel Kuettel, Richard A. Wood, And Niklas Boers

Author(s): Daniel Pals, Sebastian Bathiany, Joel Kuettel, Richard A. Wood, and Niklas Boers

A method is introduced for systematic calibration of complex dynamical system models, targeted at adjusting system stability, with applications to climate models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021007] Published Tue Apr 07, 2026.
tldr: A method for calibrating complex dynamical system models to adjust stability biases, applied to climate models.
motivation: Complex dynamical system models often have stability biases that affect their predictive accuracy; a systematic calibration method is needed.
method: The authors introduce a targeted calibration technique that adjusts model parameters to correct stability biases, demonstrated on climate models.
result: The method successfully reduces stability biases in the tested climate models, improving their fidelity.
conclusion: Targeted calibration is an effective approach for correcting stability biases in complex dynamical system models, with potential applications beyond climate science.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on surface defects and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-voltage devices; understanding its mechanism can improve reliability.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a mechanistic picture of breakdown initiation.
result: A coherent model emerges where tiny surface defects, electric stress, heat, and emitted particles interact to trigger breakdown.
conclusion: Insights from this model can help design more robust accelerator structures and other high-power technologies.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5

tldr: A review of the physics and chemistry of transplutonium elements under high pressure, focusing on their electronic properties and behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical studies of metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of pressure-induced changes in electronic structure, bonding, and phase transitions in transplutonium materials.
conclusion: High-pressure studies reveal complex behavior in transplutonium elements, but the field remains challenging due to radioactivity and electron correlation effects.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to nuclear astrophysics and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper surveys detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and discusses simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It highlights the potential for multimessenger observations to improve understanding of dense matter in neutron stars.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will become increasingly important with next-generation detectors.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of neutron star observations and the dense matter equation of state, focusing on gravitational waves and X-ray pulse profiles.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities found in neutron stars, which is not accessible in terrestrial experiments.
method: Review of recent gravitational-wave detections from binary neutron star mergers and X-ray pulse profile measurements, compared to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities are presented, showing consistency with some nuclear models but leaving uncertainties at higher densities.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine the equation of state, but current data already provide important insights into dense matter.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View

abstract:

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.

motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics research, particularly neural networks and associative memory.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture, not a technical research paper.
result: No new scientific results; discusses the evolution of ideas in physics and computation.
conclusion: Physics is a way of thinking that can lead to discoveries across disciplines.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.

motivation: To present the development and significance of Boltzmann machines, which are stochastic neural networks that learn probability distributions.
method: The lecture describes the architecture, training algorithm (contrastive divergence), and theoretical underpinnings of Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines can learn complex distributions and have been influential in deep learning, but the lecture does not present new research results.
conclusion: Boltzmann machines remain a key concept in machine learning, but the paper is a retrospective lecture, not a research contribution.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper reviews three real-space techniques to address this challenge.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete defect picture.
result: The review highlights capabilities and limitations of each technique and cases where combining them yields more comprehensive disorder characterization.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy techniques, especially when combined, provide valuable atomic-scale disorder information for semiconductor materials.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: A review of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonance phenomena.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for astrophysics but experimentally challenging due to low rates.
method: Summarizes theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: Provides an overview of the state-of-the-art in low-energy nuclear reaction theory.
conclusion: New experimental and theoretical methods are needed to study these reactions on Earth.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and self-consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, requiring periodic updates as new measurements become available.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, incorporating correlations and uncertainties to produce recommended values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for constants such as the Planck constant, elementary charge, and Boltzmann constant, along with their uncertainties, is provided.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the authoritative reference for fundamental constants, supporting precision measurements and theoretical work across physics and chemistry.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. This review presents a modern treatment of the Biot instability, integrating many standard techniques of nonlinear physics and solid mechanics, such as bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of buckling instabilities in growing soft matter using nonlinear elasticity theory.
motivation: Understanding creases and cusps in soft materials is important for morphogenesis and materials science.
method: The review integrates bifurcation theory, conformal mapping, and nonlinear elasticity to analyze the Biot instability.
result: Provides a modern treatment of buckling patterns in growing soft matter.

title: Wannier-function Software Ecosystem For Materials Simulations
authors: Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, And Giovanni Pizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Antimo Marrazzo, Sophie Beck, Elena R. Margine, Nicola Marzari, Arash A. Mostofi, Junfeng Qiao, Ivo Souza, Stepan S. Tsirkin, Jonathan R. Yates, and Giovanni Pizzi

The description of the electronic structure in terms of extended Bloch states has made it possible to understand and calculate many properties in condensed-matter physics. However, understanding and insight often require a local description, and Wannier functions provide an exact and insightful map of extended reciprocal-space Bloch states into localized real-space orbitals. Applications range far and wide, from ultra-accurate integrations to topological invariants, and their widespread uptake by the electronic-structure community has resulted in a growing and interoperable ecosystem of methods and associated software tools. This review provides a description of this ecosystem that has now become a major instrument for the electronic-structure community in its pursuit of understanding, discovering, and designing materials.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045008] Published Mon Dec 23, 2024.
tldr: A review of the Wannier-function software ecosystem for materials simulations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the methods and tools for constructing and using Wannier functions in electronic structure calculations.
method: The paper surveys the ecosystem of software packages (e.g., Wannier90) and their applications, describing the underlying theory and interoperability.
result: It catalogs the capabilities of the ecosystem, including applications to topological invariants, Berry phases, and accurate integrations.
conclusion: The Wannier-function ecosystem is a major instrument for the electronic-structure community, enabling a wide range of materials simulations.

title: Kinetic Solitary Electrostatic Structures In Collisionless Plasma: Phase-space Holes
authors: I. H. Hutchinson
abstract:
Author(s): I. H. Hutchinson

Plasma is usually taught to be a quasineutral gas of charged and neutral particles that exhibits collective behavior. However, satellites regularly observe solitary potential structures in space plasmas that are isolated positive or negative potential humps, called electron or ion holes. In the 1970s, laboratory observations were made of electron holes. This review presents an overview of the observation of these electrostatic structures and presents their origin and their stability, using analytic theory and simulations. The role of kinetically unstable velocity distributions is identified as a key driver.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045007] Published Tue Dec 10, 2024.
tldr: A review of solitary electrostatic structures (phase-space holes) in collisionless plasma, covering observations, theory, and simulations.
motivation: To understand the formation and stability of isolated potential humps observed in space plasmas, which are not explained by standard quasineutral plasma theory.
method: Review of satellite observations, laboratory experiments, analytic theory, and particle-in-cell simulations of electron and ion holes.
result: Phase-space holes arise from kinetic instabilities in velocity distributions and can be stable over long timescales.
conclusion: Kinetic effects are essential for explaining these structures, and further study is needed to connect them to broader plasma phenomena.

title: Observable Gravitational Wave Strain At Second Order

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221402] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper resolves the ambiguity in associating gravitational waves with transverse-traceless components at second order in perturbation theory by computing the detector response to second order.
motivation: The ambiguity in defining gravitational waves at second order in perturbation theory needed resolution to correctly interpret observable signals.
method: The authors compute the detector response to second order in perturbation theory for the first time.
result: They show that the observable strain measured by a detector corresponds to the transverse-traceless metric perturbation at second order.
conclusion: The ambiguity is resolved, confirming that the transverse-traceless component is the correct observable gravitational wave strain at second order.

title: $n=8$ Shell Breaking In $^{12}\mathrm{Be}$ From A Single-Particle Perspective

title: Electron Affinity Of The Carbon Dimer From Threshold Photodetachment Spectroscopy
authors: Sruthi Purushu Melath, Michael Hauck, Christine Lochmann, Robert Wild, Timothy P. Softley, Katrin Dulitz, And Roland Wester
abstract:

tldr: This paper measures the electron affinity of the carbon dimer using threshold photodetachment spectroscopy of trapped anions.

title: One-Dimensional Brownian Motion On Unpatterned Two-Dimensional Crystal Surfaces
authors: Ruisheng Zhao, Wanlin Guo, And Hu Qiu
abstract:

motivation: Conventional 1D Brownian motion on surfaces requires physical tracks; this work explores whether intrinsic surface properties can guide motion without patterning.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of a monolayer polymeric nanoflake on a crystal surface.
result: The nanoflake exhibits persistent 1D Brownian motion along a specific direction on the unpatterned surface.
conclusion: Intrinsic surface anisotropy can enable 1D diffusion without prefabricated tracks, offering a new mechanism for directed motion.

We investigate how structural ordering, i.e., crystallization, affects the flow of bidisperse granular materials in a quasi-two-dimensional silo. By systematically varying the mass fraction of two particle sizes, we finely tune the degree of local order. Using high-speed imaging and kinematic modeli…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 228201] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the relationship between structural ordering and diffusion in granular flow, a topic in soft matter physics.
motivation: Understanding how crystallization affects granular flow is important for industrial processes and fundamental physics of dense granular materials.
method: Bidisperse granular materials are flowed in a quasi-2D silo; high-speed imaging and kinematic modeling are used to measure local order and diffusion length.
result: A correlation is found between the degree of structural order and the diffusion length, indicating that ordering suppresses diffusion.
conclusion: Structural ordering plays a key role in granular flow dynamics, with implications for predicting flow behavior in granular systems.

title: Quasinormal Modes Ratios As Agnostic Test Of General Relativity
authors: Nicola Franchini
abstract:

In this Letter, we provide a novel test of general relativity based on ringdown analysis. tldr: This paper proposes a test of general relativity using quasinormal mode ratios from black hole ringdown, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide a novel, agnostic test of general relativity based on ringdown analysis of gravitational waves.
method: The postmerger signal is fitted with a superposition of damped sinusoids, and the ratio of frequencies of at least two detected modes is computed.
result: The test is demonstrated on agnostic models, showing how deviations from general relativity can be constrained.
conclusion: The method offers a robust way to test general relativity using ringdown signals without assuming specific alternative theories.

result: First measurements of differential cross sections and charge asymmetry for top quarks in the forward region.
conclusion: The results provide new constraints on parton distribution functions and test QCD predictions.

authors: Wu Wen, Jing Li, And Yunquan Liu

result: The structure can function as a nanoscale undulator, producing tunable coherent radiation in the femtosecond regime at the nanoscale.
conclusion: This approach offers a new way to generate coherent radiation with high spatial and temporal resolution, potentially useful for ultrafast spectroscopy and imaging.

title: Existent Condition Of Partially Wet State In Capillary Tubes

motivation: Conventional quadratic nonlinear interactions with femtosecond lasers suffer from group-velocity mismatch (GVM) that limits phase-matching bandwidth. The authors aim to show that GVM can be harnessed to enable ultrafast parametric interactions without requiring broadband phase-matching.
method: The authors theoretically and experimentally demonstrate a parametric process where nonvanished GVMs are exploited to achieve efficient ultrafast frequency conversion.
result: They show that by allowing GVM, the phase-matching bandwidth can be significantly increased, enabling ultrafast parametric interactions without the need for broadband phase-matching techniques.
conclusion: The work challenges the conventional view of GVM as detrimental and opens new possibilities for ultrafast nonlinear optics.

title: Collective Dynamics Of Natural Killer Cells Interacting With Cancer And Fibroblast Cells
authors: Yun-Xuan Zhang, Shu-Chen Liu, And Lin I
abstract:
Author(s): Yun-Xuan Zhang, Shu-Chen Liu, and Lin I

The authors tested the response of natural killer cells cocultured with cancer cells and with fibroblasts. They found that natural killer cells targeted the cancer cells, but not fibroblasts. The natural killer cells clustered around cancer cells and promoted apoptosis, whereas they scouted around fibroblasts and did not form large aggregates. Generality of these responses could be established by testing additional normal cell types and tumor lines.

motivation: Understanding how natural killer cells distinguish between cancer cells and normal cells is important for immunotherapy.
method: The authors cocultured natural killer cells with cancer cells and fibroblasts, observing cell clustering and apoptosis.
result: Natural killer cells clustered around cancer cells and promoted apoptosis, but only scouted around fibroblasts without forming aggregates.
conclusion: The response is specific to cancer cells, suggesting potential for targeted immunotherapy.

conclusion: The nonlinear dynamics could be exploited to optimize thruster performance, but no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

conclusion: Differential dynamic microscopy is a powerful tool for studying Lévy flights in active matter systems.

method: Simulations of ICF implosions are performed, demonstrating the onset of Rayleigh-Bénard convection near the fuel-ablator interface.
result: Rayleigh-Bénard convection occurs and can cause convective heating within the cold fuel, potentially degrading implosion performance.
conclusion: Rayleigh-Bénard convection is a relevant instability mechanism in ICF that should be considered in design and analysis.

conclusion: The proposed framework effectively captures stochastic cellular dynamics from unpaired snapshots, offering a powerful tool for single-cell analysis.

result: Identifies pathway redundancy as a mechanism for intrinsic noise suppression in protein allostery.

title: Optimal Ambition In Business, Politics, And Life
authors: Ekaterina Landgren, Ryan E. Langendorf, And Matthew G. Burgess

“The perfect is the enemy of the good.” The authors develop a search model that formalizes this adage. method: A mathematical search model is constructed and analyzed, with predictions tested against real-world data from online dating and college admissions.
result: Optimal ambition targets outcomes that are finite but strictly larger than the mean of available rewards.
conclusion: The model provides a formal framework for setting ambition levels in various domains, with empirical support from two case studies.

title: Comment On “Experimental Demonstration Of Electric Power Generation From Earth's Rotation Through Its Own Magnetic Field”

abstract:
Author(s): Yiyang Ye and Jie Lin

Understanding how cells sense mechanical cues and regulate migration is crucial in the development, fibrosis, and oncogenesis processes. However, a comprehensive physical picture of cell migration remains lacking, given the diverse environmental properties and cell physiologies. Here, we generalize …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023216] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell migration modes on substrates with varying stiffness and actin polymerization speed, identifying gripping, slipping, and stick-slip regimes.
motivation: Understanding how cells sense mechanical cues and regulate migration is crucial for development, fibrosis, and oncogenesis, but a comprehensive physical picture is lacking.
method: The authors generalize a physical model of cell migration incorporating substrate properties and actin polymerization speed, and analyze the resulting migration modes.
result: They find that substrate stiffness and actin polymerization speed dictate universal modes of cell migration: gripping, slipping, and stick-slip.
conclusion: The work provides a unified physical framework for cell migration, which may help in understanding related biological processes.

title: Erratum: Electron Beams Traversing Spherical Nanoparticles: Analytic And Numerical Treatment [Phys. Rev. Research 6, 013239 (2024)]

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 029002] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting a previous paper on electron beams interacting with spherical nanoparticles, with no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The original paper presented analytic and numerical methods for electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) in spherical nanoparticles; this erratum corrects errors in that work.
method: The erratum likely corrects equations or numerical results from the original publication.
result: Corrections to the previously published results are provided.
conclusion: The corrected results should be used in place of the original ones.

title: Directional Asymmetry In Strong-field Ionization Induced By A Terahertz-assisted Laser Pulse
authors: F. Žgalj, A. S. Jašarević, D. Habibović, And D. B. Milošević
abstract:
Author(s): F. Žgalj, A. S. Jašarević, D. Habibović, and D. B. Milošević

We investigate directional asymmetry in strong-field ionization driven by a few-cycle near-infrared laser pulse assisted by a time-delayed terahertz (THz) pulse. Within the strong-field approximation, we show that the relative delay between the laser and THz pulses provides an efficient control para…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023211] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies directional asymmetry in strong-field ionization using a terahertz-assisted laser pulse, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand and control electron dynamics in strong-field ionization using a THz pulse.
method: Theoretical analysis within the strong-field approximation, varying the time delay between laser and THz pulses.
result: The relative delay provides efficient control of directional asymmetry in ionization.
conclusion: The work contributes to attosecond science and strong-field physics, not to the user's research areas.

title: Super-resonance: Breaking The Bandwidth Limit Of Resonant Modes And Its Application To Flow Control
authors: Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, And Mahmoud I. Hussein
abstract:
Author(s): Adam R. Harris, Armin Kianfar, David Roca, Daniel Yago, Christoph Brehm, and Mahmoud I. Hussein

Super-resonance maintains a broadband out-of-phase response well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling broadband flow stabilization among other applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021045] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces super-resonance, a phenomenon that breaks the bandwidth limit of resonant modes, and applies it to flow control.
motivation: Conventional resonance has a limited bandwidth, which restricts applications like flow stabilization. The authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically and numerically demonstrate super-resonance in a system of coupled resonators, showing a broadband out-of-phase response beyond the usual bandwidth.
result: Super-resonance achieves a broadband response that persists well beyond the characteristic bandwidth of conventional resonance, enabling effective flow stabilization.
conclusion: Super-resonance provides a new mechanism for broadband resonant behavior with potential applications in flow control and other areas.

title: Stretching Theory Of Hookean Metashells
authors: Luca Giomi
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Giomi

A continuum theory that describes how mechanical metamaterials deform on surfaces takes the form of the Schrödinger equation and provides a different path for materials design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021035] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: A continuum theory for mechanical metamaterials on surfaces is formulated analogously to the Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework for designing mechanical metamaterials that deform on curved surfaces.
method: The author derives a continuum theory that maps the deformation of Hookean metashells to a Schrödinger-like equation.
result: The theory provides a new mathematical description of metashell mechanics, enabling novel material design.
conclusion: The work offers a different path for materials design by linking mechanics to quantum-like equations.

title: Using Folded Proteins As Mechanically Well-Defined Units To Understand Fatigue Fracture In Hydrogels: Bridging Single Molecule And Bulk Studies
authors: Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, And Hai Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Dong, Puyu Cao, Huiyan Chen, Yu Zhang, Ying Li, Bin Chen, Yi Cao, and Hai Lei

A force-response model helps understand fatigue behavior and provides a design strategy for fatigue resistant hydrogels and soft materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021031] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies fatigue fracture in hydrogels using folded proteins as mechanically well-defined units, bridging single-molecule and bulk experiments.
motivation: Understanding fatigue fracture in soft materials is crucial for designing durable hydrogels, but the molecular mechanisms are poorly understood.
method: The authors use folded proteins as model units to probe mechanical fatigue at the single-molecule level and relate it to bulk hydrogel behavior through a force-response model.
result: They identify key molecular determinants of fatigue and propose design strategies for fatigue-resistant hydrogels.
conclusion: The work provides a molecular-level understanding of fatigue fracture and offers practical guidelines for creating tougher soft materials.

title: Hydroplasticity Of Nanocrystal Films Induced By Mesopore Change
authors: Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, And Kai Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Siyuan Liu, Yonggui Wang, Yu Yin, Xintong Meng, Zhen Lang, and Kai Zhang

A vapor training process allows for improved plasticity and better shaping of wood-derived films.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021026] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the hydroplasticity of nanocrystal films induced by mesopore change, focusing on wood-derived films and vapor training processes.
motivation: To improve the plasticity and shaping of wood-derived films for practical applications.
method: A vapor training process is used to induce mesopore changes in nanocrystal films.
result: The vapor training process improves plasticity and enables better shaping of the films.
conclusion: The method offers a way to enhance the mechanical properties of wood-derived films.

title: Cell Bulging And Extrusion In A Three-Dimensional Bubbly Vertex Model For Curved Epithelial Sheets
authors: Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, And Ulrich S. Schwarz
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Drozdowski, Büşra Kocameşe-Tamgac𝚤, Kim E. Boonekamp, Michael Boutros, and Ulrich S. Schwarz

Cells at topological defects in curved epithelial sheets experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021023] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cell bulging and extrusion in curved epithelial sheets using a three-dimensional bubbly vertex model.
motivation: Understanding mechanical forces at topological defects in curved epithelial tissues, which are relevant to developmental biology and disease.
method: A three-dimensional bubbly vertex model is developed to simulate curved epithelial sheets and analyze cell dynamics.
result: Cells at topological defects experience mechanical forces that facilitate extrusion, with bulging behavior observed.
conclusion: The model provides insights into the role of geometry and mechanics in epithelial tissue remodeling.

title: Seeing New Depths: Three-Dimensional Flow Of A Free-Swimming Alga
authors: Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, And Xiang Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Gregorius Pradipta, Wanho Lee, Van Tran, Kyle Welch, Santosh K. Sankar, Yongsam Kim, Satish Kumar, Xin Yong, Jiarong Hong, Sookkyung Lim, and Xiang Cheng

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021019] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental 3D measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga, revealing unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
motivation: Understanding microhydrodynamics of swimming microorganisms is important for biology and fluid dynamics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: Experimental three-dimensional flow measurements around a free-swimming alga.
result: Discovery of unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena.
conclusion: The findings expand understanding of microhydrodynamics with biological implications.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A review of hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and QCD.
motivation: To understand strong interaction mechanisms such as quark confinement and gluon binding through charmonium decays and searches for new hadrons.
method: Review of experimental results from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII on hadron production in e+e- collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs.
result: Summarizes current progress and highlights recent advances from BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: Hadron spectroscopy in open-charm channels provides crucial tests of QCD and continues to yield new insights.

title: Editorial: A Tribute To The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Véronique van Elewyck And Dietrich Belitz
abstract:
Author(s): Véronique Van Elewyck and Dietrich Belitz

Three Colloquia honor the Arecibo Observatory’s legacy, exploring its revolutionary impact on planetary radar studies, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 010001] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: An editorial tribute to the Arecibo Observatory, summarizing its legacy in planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.
motivation: To honor the Arecibo Observatory's contributions and reflect on its impact across multiple scientific fields.
method: The paper is an editorial compilation of colloquia, not a research study with a specific method.
result: No new research results; it is a retrospective overview.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory had a revolutionary impact on planetary radar, radio astronomy, and geospace science.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A review of planetary radar observations at Arecibo Observatory, covering techniques and scientific results for Solar System bodies.
motivation: To summarize the legacy of the most sensitive planetary radar system, which provided unique subsurface and surface data for planets, moons, and asteroids.
method: Colloquium-style review of radar techniques and key observational campaigns from the late 1990s to 2020.
result: Highlights Arecibo's contributions to understanding Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids/comets.
conclusion: Arecibo's radar system was a unique and powerful tool for planetary science, and its loss leaves a gap in observational capabilities.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to radio astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its scientific impact over five decades.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from Arecibo's upgrades and observations.
result: Highlights Arecibo's major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo was a transformative instrument in radio astronomy, and its loss is significant for the field.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews advances in geospace science made using the Arecibo Observatory's radar and lidar instruments, focusing on ionospheric physics and space weather.
motivation: To summarize the scientific contributions of the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric research.
method: Review of incoherent scatter radar technique and results from Arecibo's suite of instruments including lidars and optical sensors.
result: Key advances in plasma physics, space weather, metal atom layers, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling are highlighted.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in geospace science, and its legacy continues through ongoing analysis of its data.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: The rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is poorly understood; controlled experiments are needed.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud processes.
result: Convection-cloud chambers can generate turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation, bridging laboratory and atmospheric scales.
conclusion: These chambers offer a promising approach to resolving the precipitation bottleneck in cloud physics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection in multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: Core collapse supernovae are rare events that provide unique insights into stellar physics and neutron star formation; detecting gravitational waves alongside photons and neutrinos would enable multimessenger studies.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods and parameter estimation for ground-based laser interferometers.
result: It presents the latest predictions for gravitational wave signatures from core collapse supernovae and outlines strategies for multimessenger observation.
conclusion: The detection of a Galactic supernova would be a landmark event, and coordinated multimessenger observations are essential to fully exploit the scientific potential.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a tension between the dipole in the cosmic microwave background and that in large-scale structure, challenging the cosmological principle.
motivation: To test the foundational cosmological principle of isotropy and homogeneity by comparing the dipole in galaxy/quasar catalogs with the CMB dipole.
method: Analysis of large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole, including checks for biases and systematics.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the matter dipole and the CMB dipole, which cannot be explained by known systematic effects.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may indicate a violation of the cosmological principle or require modifications to the standard ΛCDM model.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sectors and halo dynamics.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and test self-interacting dark matter models using astrophysical observations.
method: Review of observational constraints from galaxies to large-scale structures, comparing predictions of self-interacting dark matter with standard cold dark matter.
result: Summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and outlines future observational prospects.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable alternative to cold dark matter, with ongoing and upcoming surveys expected to provide tighter constraints.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond-Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space, motivating a review of viable models and future discovery potential.
method: The paper surveys theoretical models and experimental search channels, projecting sensitivities for the High-Luminosity LHC.
result: Stringent bounds on supersymmetric particles are summarized, and discovery prospects for various scenarios are presented.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable but increasingly constrained; the HL-LHC offers the best chance for discovery in the coming decade.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models and experimental data from the last decade on nuclear reaction rates, plasma effects, and atomic physics in the solar interior.
result: Updated nuclear reaction rates and improved solar models are presented, with comparisons to neutrino and helioseismic observations.
conclusion: The review consolidates recent advances in solar fusion physics, providing a benchmark for stellar modeling.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: A review of gas bubble dynamics in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and surfactants.
motivation: Gas bubbles are important in many natural and industrial processes, but their dynamics are complex due to deformability and interactions.
method: The paper reviews experimental and theoretical advances over the past 20 years, focusing on key factors like turbulence, rheology, and electrolytes.
result: It highlights how added mass, deformability, and surfactants affect bubble motion and interactions.
conclusion: The review provides insights to improve modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on polar active particles that align their orientation with their velocity.
motivation: To understand and unify the diverse behaviors arising from self-alignment in active matter, with potential applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment, presenting a unified mathematical and conceptual framework.
result: Self-alignment leads to novel single-particle and collective phenomena, such as orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental mechanism in active matter that can be harnessed for designing new materials and robotic systems.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, a biomedical imaging technique, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Advanced imaging methods are needed for biological and clinical insight; optoacoustic imaging offers deep-tissue optical contrast with high resolution.
method: The paper reviews the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, where short laser pulses absorbed by tissue generate ultrasound waves detected externally.
result: The technique enables noninvasive imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, and multimodal combinations with optical microscopy are discussed.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical research, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Using Gravitational Waves To See The First Second Of The Universe
authors: Rishav Roshan And Graham White
abstract:
Author(s): Rishav Roshan and Graham White

Gravitational waves open a unique window on the earliest times in cosmology because the dense primordial plasma, impenetrable to light or neutrinos, is transparent to gravitational waves up to the instant of the birth of the Universe. This review discusses the possible signals from the phase transitions, topological defects, and other cosmological sources, as well as a range of strategies for detection of the stochastic gravitational waves produced by the earliest events in the history of the Universe.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015001] Published Wed Jan 08, 2025.
tldr: A review of using gravitational waves to probe the early universe, focusing on phase transitions and topological defects.
motivation: To explore how gravitational waves can reveal physics from the first second after the Big Bang, which is opaque to electromagnetic radiation.
method: Review of theoretical models for gravitational wave sources (phase transitions, topological defects) and detection strategies.
result: Summarizes potential signals and detection methods for stochastic gravitational waves from early universe events.
conclusion: Gravitational waves offer a unique probe of early universe cosmology, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
